You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/manufacturing-mrp (dev merged; manufacturing masters 8.1 + production orders 8.2 done). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite). This is the FINAL Phase 8 task; it completes manufacturing.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md PP (MRP = PARTIAL "the core deterministic run — sales-order demand + reorder points exploded against supply, producing planned orders — is planned; exception messages, MRP areas, multi-plant, net-change, MRP-Live performance are NOT"; capacity = PARTIAL "evaluation only — rough load vs available hours per work center; no leveling/finite scheduling"); docs/architecture.md D-013 (idempotency), D-014 (pagination), D-015 (QuantityType), D-029 (opaque ids via queries), D-022/D-025, PERFORMANCE §2 (the run is BULK/set-based, no per-item N+1) + §3 (a large run is a BACKGROUND JOB — mirror bank-import/depreciation), D-032 (the job core). Then read the EXACT code to integrate with + mirror:
- backend/app/core/jobs.py (register_job, submit_job, the JobScheduler — the MRP run submits as a job above a threshold; mirror finance/service/depreciation.py's job usage + 6.4B reorder scan).
- backend/app/modules/procurement/service/reorder.py (6.4B reorder scan: reads inventory/queries.items_below_reorder_point and creates DRAFT requisitions — MRP is the demand-driven superset; reuse the items_below_reorder_point query + the dedup approach) + procurement/queries.py (open_incoming_quantity — supply from open POs) + procurement requisition create (a planned BUY order converts to a procurement requisition — cross-module: §5 means MRP can't call procurement service; either MRP produces a planned-purchase order and procurement converts it, OR MRP publishes an event procurement handles; mirror how 6.4B did it / how cross-module creation works elsewhere — DECIDE and document).
- backend/app/modules/sales/queries.py (open sales-order demand — committed/undelivered order line quantities = the demand source; find/add a query `open_sales_demand(item_id)` or `committed_quantity` already exists — reuse; MRP demand = sum of undelivered confirmed sales-order line quantities per item).
- backend/app/modules/inventory/queries.py (total_on_hand, items_below_reorder_point, item reorder_point/reorder_quantity) — supply (on-hand) + reorder demand.
- backend/app/modules/manufacturing/ — queries.py (get_active_bom_for_item, bom_components — to EXPLODE a manufactured item's demand into component demand; get_item costing/make-or-buy: how do we know make vs buy? An item is MAKE if it has an active BOM, else BUY — document this rule), service/production_orders.py (create_production_order — converting a planned MAKE order creates a real production order, manufacturing-internal, fine), models (ProductionOrder, ProductionOrderOperation with planned_minutes — the capacity load source), constants.
- backend/tests/modules/manufacturing/{factories.py, production_factories.py, conftest.py} + sales/inventory/procurement factories (to seed demand: a confirmed sales order; on-hand; an item below reorder; a BOM for explosion).
Latest migration = 0033.

CRITICAL §5: MRP READS across modules via their queries (sales/inventory/procurement/manufacturing queries) — never their service (except manufacturing's OWN service to create production orders, which is intra-module). A planned BUY order becoming a procurement requisition is cross-module: do it via the event bus OR by procurement reading manufacturing's planned-buy output (a query) and converting — choose the cleaner one and document in DECISIONS.md D-049. Verify manufacturing imports only other modules' queries + events.

TASK — PLAN 8.3: MRP run (demand + reorder vs supply → planned orders) + rough capacity check. Build:

1. manufacturing/constants.py additions: PlannedOrderType (MAKE|BUY), PlannedOrderStatus (PLANNED|FIRMED|CONVERTED|CANCELLED), MrpRunStatus (RUNNING|COMPLETED|FAILED — or reuse the job status). Permissions manufacturing.mrp.read/.run, manufacturing.planned_order.read/.manage (firm/convert/cancel). Sequence for planned orders if numbered (PLN-…) — or they're ephemeral planning output keyed by run; give the RUN a number 'manufacturing.mrp_run' (MRP-…). Doc types as needed. Job type 'manufacturing.mrp_run'.
2. manufacturing/models (models/mrp.py; re-export): 
   - `MrpRun` (`mfg_mrp_runs`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin?; run_number, status, run_date, warehouse_id (opaque — MRP scope is a warehouse, or tenant-wide; pick warehouse-scoped or all — document; tenant-wide simplest for v1), demand_source notes, planned_make_count / planned_buy_count, notes, completed_at. 
   - `PlannedOrder` (`mfg_planned_orders`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin; mrp_run_id (composite tenant_fk — the run that produced it; planned orders are regenerated each run — a re-run supersedes prior PLANNED orders that weren't FIRMED/CONVERTED, document the regeneration policy), item_id (opaque), order_type (MAKE|BUY), quantity (QuantityType — the net requirement to produce/buy), due_date (Date nullable — from the demand), status, source notes (why: net of demand X − supply Y), converted_document_id (nullable — the production order / requisition created on conversion, via docflow), level (int — the BOM explosion level, for ordering: level-0 finished goods first). Index (tenant, mrp_run_id), (tenant, item_id, status).
   - `CapacityLoad` (`mfg_capacity_loads`, the rough capacity check output): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin; mrp_run_id (composite tenant_fk), work_center_id (composite tenant_fk to mfg_work_centers), planned_load_minutes (QuantityType — sum of planned-order operation minutes routed through this work center), available_minutes (QuantityType — work_center capacity_hours_per_day × efficiency × the planning horizon days), utilization_percent (Numeric/MoneyType), is_overloaded (bool — load > available). UNIQUE(tenant, mrp_run_id, work_center_id).
3. manufacturing/service (service/mrp.py + mrp_capacity.py + planned_orders.py, each <400):
   - `run_mrp(session, tenant_id, run_date, warehouse?, horizon_days)` — the deterministic engine, SET-BASED (PERFORMANCE §2): 
     a) Gather DEMAND per item: open sales-order demand (sum undelivered confirmed sales-order line qty per item, via sales/queries) + reorder-point shortfall (items where on-hand < reorder_point → demand = reorder_quantity, via inventory/queries.items_below_reorder_point). 
     b) Gather SUPPLY per item: on-hand (inventory) + open production orders (manufacturing, un-finished quantity) + open POs (procurement open_incoming_quantity). 
     c) Net requirement per item = max(0, demand − supply). 
     d) For each item with a net requirement: if MAKE (has an active BOM) → create a planned MAKE order for the net qty AND EXPLODE its BOM to generate dependent DEMAND for its components (multi-level: process items level by level, finished goods (level 0) first, then their components (level 1), etc., with a visited-set/level cap to prevent infinite loops on a (guarded-but-defensive) cycle); if BUY (no active BOM) → create a planned BUY order. 
     e) The explosion must be LEVEL-ORDERED and accumulate component demand across all parents (a component used by two finished goods sums). Use a low-level-code / iterative leveling approach; keep it bounded (max levels, e.g. 20) and set-based per level (no per-item query storms — batch the BOM/on-hand/demand lookups per level).
     f) Write the MrpRun + PlannedOrder rows (bulk insert). Regeneration: delete/supersede prior PLANNED (un-firmed) planned orders for the tenant before writing new ones (a fresh net plan), keep FIRMED/CONVERTED ones and net them as supply. Document.
     Run as a BACKGROUND JOB ('manufacturing.mrp_run') above a threshold (e.g. >50 items or always-job since it scans everything — mirror depreciation/bank: submit the job, return 202 + job id; a tiny tenant could run inline, but MRP scanning all items is naturally a job — make it ALWAYS a job for consistency, OR inline under a small item count; document). Idempotent at the endpoint.
   - `rough_capacity_check(session, tenant_id, mrp_run_id, horizon_days)` — for the run's planned MAKE orders + open production orders, sum each work center's operation load (planned_minutes) and compare to available (capacity_hours/day × efficiency × horizon_days × 60); write CapacityLoad rows; flag overloaded. Set-based.
   - `firm_planned_order` / `convert_planned_order(planned_order_id)` — a MAKE planned order → create a real production order (manufacturing.create_production_order, intra-module); a BUY planned order → a procurement requisition (cross-module — via the §5-clean mechanism you chose: event or procurement-reads-planned-buy; implement the conversion). Link docflow planned-order→converted-document. cancel.
   - `planned_orders_for_run`, `capacity_for_run` reads.
4. manufacturing/queries.py additions: planned_orders, get_mrp_run, open_production_order_supply(item_id) (un-finished production qty — supply side). 
5. manufacturing/events.py: if a planned BUY order converts to a requisition via event, add the event; else none.
6. manufacturing/router (mrp_router sibling, mounted): POST /mrp/runs (run MRP; manufacturing.mrp.run; 202 + job id; idempotent), GET /mrp/runs (paginated) + /{id} (+ summary), GET /mrp/runs/{id}/planned-orders (paginated, filter type/status), GET /mrp/runs/{id}/capacity (the capacity loads, overloaded flagged), POST /planned-orders/{id}/firm, POST /planned-orders/{id}/convert (idempotent), POST /planned-orders/{id}/cancel. Permission-guard. PERFORMANCE §6. Mount.
7. Migration 0034_manufacturing_mrp.py (down_revision 0033): mfg_mrp_runs + mfg_planned_orders + mfg_capacity_loads + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
8. docs/modules/manufacturing.md: MRP section (the demand sources, supply sources, net-requirement formula, level-ordered multi-level explosion, MAKE-vs-BUY = has-active-BOM, planned orders + regeneration policy, conversion to production orders/requisitions, the rough capacity check, background-job execution, what's deferred per parity). DECISIONS.md D-049 (MRP demand/supply sources + net formula; MAKE=has-BOM/BUY=no-BOM; level-ordered explosion with cap; planned-order regeneration policy; the §5-clean planned-BUY→requisition conversion mechanism; MRP always a background job).
9. Tests: test_mrp.py + test_mrp_api.py + test_capacity.py: a deterministic scenario — a finished item with a 2-level BOM, a confirmed sales order creating demand, some on-hand reducing net, a component below reorder point; run MRP → assert the planned MAKE order for the finished item (net = demand − on-hand), the exploded component demand → planned orders for sub-components (MAKE if they have BOMs, BUY if not) at the right quantities and levels, supply (an open PO / open production order) reducing net; reorder-point items get a planned BUY; regeneration (re-run supersedes un-firmed planned orders, keeps firmed); convert a planned MAKE order → a real production order (assert it exists + docflow); convert a planned BUY → a procurement requisition; the rough capacity check flags an overloaded work center (planned load > available) and not an underloaded one; the run is a background job (202 + job completes); RBAC (mrp.run vs planned_order.manage), idempotency, pagination, tenant isolation. Use set-based seeding; assert the run executes a BOUNDED number of queries per BOM level (not per-item N+1) — a query-counter bound on the run. HEED #53.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; EVERY file <400 lines (packages/sibling-routers from the start); comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 8.3 (note Phase 8 / Manufacturing COMPLETE) + DECISIONS.md D-049. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. §5) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the MRP demand/supply/net model + the level-ordered explosion + MAKE-vs-BUY rule, the planned-order regeneration policy, the §5-clean planned-BUY→requisition mechanism, the capacity-check formula, the background-job execution, the bounded-query (no N+1) approach, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

31	  ``get_active_routing_for_item`` resolve (8.2/8.3 read this). Activating a version that becomes the
32	  new default first demotes the previously-default ACTIVE version's ``is_default`` flag.
33	- **INACTIVE** — retired: a once-ACTIVE version superseded by a newer one; kept for history /
34	  referenceability, never deleted.

41	needs A) is a 8.3 explosion-time concern (the explosion carries a visited set + depth cap, the

1	"""Background jobs (PLAN 4P.5, PERFORMANCE §3 — closes #26): registry, submit, in-process runner.
2	
3	Long-running operations (FX revaluation, payment runs, statement imports >1k lines, MRP) must
4	never execute inside a request that can hit a proxy timeout. The pattern:
5	
6	1. A module registers a handler at import time::
7	
8	       @register_job("finance.fx_revaluation")
9	       async def handler(session, tenant_id, payload: dict) -> dict: ...
10	
11	   The registry is CODE-DEFINED, exactly like the permission registry (core/rbac.py): a job type
12	   exists because a handler for it is in the codebase, never as data.
13	2. The endpoint calls ``submit_job(session, ...)`` INSIDE its ``run_in_uow`` work — the PENDING
14	   row commits atomically with the request (and with the D-013 idempotency capture, so a replayed
15	   Idempotency-Key returns the SAME job id) — then, strictly AFTER the uow commit, calls
16	   ``schedule_job(job.id, session_factory)`` and returns ``202 {job_id, status}``.
17	3. The client polls ``GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`` (core/jobs_router.py) until COMPLETED/FAILED.
18	
19	**The runner** (``_execute_job``) opens its OWN session from the factory the submitter passed —
20	in production that is the request's ``get_session_factory`` dependency (the app factory), in
21	tests the per-test-engine factory the conftest override injects, so the runner always lands in
22	the same database as the submit. It restores the submitting context: ``tenant_context(tenant_id)``
23	(D-007 — handler reads/writes are tenant-filtered and stamped) and the D-010 actor ContextVar from
24	``submitted_by_user_id`` (handler writes are audited with the submitting user as actor). It marks
25	RUNNING (own commit), then runs the handler inside ``run_in_uow`` so domain events + audit behave
26	EXACTLY as in-request; the COMPLETED status + result are set inside the same uow, so business
27	writes and the terminal status commit atomically. On any exception the uow rolls the work back
28	and the runner commits only the FAILED status + error string.
29	
30	**Scheduling happens post-commit by contract** (the router calls ``schedule_job`` after
31	``run_in_uow`` returns), so the runner never races the submitting transaction's visibility.
32	
33	**Concurrency cap:** at most ``MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS`` handlers run at once (an asyncio semaphore,
34	created lazily PER EVENT LOOP because asyncio primitives bind to their first loop and tests run
35	one loop per test), so a burst of jobs cannot starve the event loop or the DB pool.
36	
37	**Swap seam:** submitters call ``schedule_job``, which delegates to the module ``scheduler``
38	bound to the ``JobScheduler`` Protocol — the same pattern as the D-011 event bus singleton. A
39	real queue (arq/celery) replaces that one binding (its ``schedule`` enqueues the job id and its
40	workers own their own engine, ignoring ``session_factory``) with zero submitter changes.
41	
42	**Not audited (documented exclusion):** ``Job`` rows are request-control infrastructure with
43	high status churn (PENDING→RUNNING→COMPLETED per job), like ``RefreshSession`` and
44	``IdempotencyKey`` — auditing them would be noise. The BUSINESS writes a handler makes are
45	audited as usual through the shared session.
46	"""
47	
48	import asyncio
49	import logging
50	import uuid
51	import weakref
52	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
53	from datetime import UTC, datetime
54	from enum import StrEnum
55	from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
56	
57	import sqlalchemy as sa
58	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker
59	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
60	
61	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx
62	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
63	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
64	from app.core.models import (
65	    JSON_VARIANT,
66	    Base,
67	    TenantMixin,
68	    TimestampMixin,
69	    UuidPKMixin,
70	    tenant_fk,
71	)
72	from app.core.tenancy import system_context, tenant_context
73	
74	logger = logging.getLogger("atlas")
75	
76	MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS = 4
77	# The error column is bounded; handler exception text is truncated to fit (D-010 precedent:
78	# capped values beat an unbounded text column on a high-churn table).
79	_ERROR_MAX_CHARS = 2000
80	
81	
82	class JobStatus(StrEnum):
83	    PENDING = "PENDING"
84	    RUNNING = "RUNNING"
85	    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
86	    FAILED = "FAILED"

89	class Job(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
90	    """One background-job execution (PLAN 4P.5). NOT ``AuditMixin`` — see module docstring.
91	
92	    ``submitted_by_user_id`` is attribution metadata like ``core_audit_log.actor_user_id``
93	    (plain nullable Uuid, no FK/index): the runner copies it into the actor ContextVar so the
94	    handler's audited writes carry the submitting user."""
95	
96	    __tablename__ = "core_jobs"
97	    __table_args__ = (
98	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
99	        # Both composites lead with tenant_id (D-022 convention keys on column 0 — name them
100	        # explicitly). Read paths: the polling list filtered by status, and "runs of one job
101	        # type over time" (also the list's job_type filter).
102	        sa.Index("ix_core_jobs_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
103	        sa.Index(
104	            "ix_core_jobs_tenant_id_job_type_created_at", "tenant_id", "job_type", "created_at"
105	        ),
106	    )
107	
108	    job_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
109	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
110	        sa.String(20), nullable=False, default=JobStatus.PENDING.value
111	    )
112	    payload: Mapped[Any] = mapped_column(JSON_VARIANT, nullable=False, default=dict)
113	    result: Mapped[Any] = mapped_column(JSON_VARIANT, nullable=True)
114	    error: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(_ERROR_MAX_CHARS), nullable=True)
115	    submitted_by_user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
116	    started_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
117	    finished_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)

120	# --- Registry (code-defined, like permissions) ----------------------------------
121	
122	# A handler runs inside run_in_uow on the runner's session, under the submitting tenant context;
123	# its dict return value becomes ``job.result`` (must be JSON-serializable).
124	JobHandler = Callable[[AsyncSession, uuid.UUID, dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[dict[str, Any]]]
125	
126	_registry: dict[str, JobHandler] = {}
127	
128	
129	def register_job(job_type: str) -> Callable[[JobHandler], JobHandler]:
130	    """Decorator registering ``handler`` for ``job_type`` at module import (idempotent for the
131	    same function; a second DIFFERENT handler for one key is a wiring bug and raises)."""
132	
133	    def decorator(handler: JobHandler) -> JobHandler:
134	        existing = _registry.get(job_type)
135	        if existing is not None and existing is not handler:
136	            raise ValueError(f"Job type {job_type!r} is already registered")
137	        _registry[job_type] = handler
138	        return handler
139	
140	    return decorator
141	
142	
143	def registered_job_types() -> tuple[str, ...]:
144	    return tuple(sorted(_registry))

146	
147	# --- Submit ----------------------------------------------------------------------
148	
149	
150	async def submit_job(
151	    session: AsyncSession,
152	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
153	    job_type: str,
154	    payload: dict[str, Any],
155	    submitted_by: uuid.UUID | None = None,
156	) -> Job:
157	    """Insert a PENDING job row (flushed, NOT committed — the caller's ``run_in_uow`` commits it
158	    atomically with the rest of the request, e.g. the idempotency capture). Rejects an
159	    unregistered ``job_type`` up front (422). The caller schedules execution AFTER its uow
160	    commit via ``schedule_job(job.id, session_factory)``."""
161	    if job_type not in _registry:
162	        raise ValidationFailedError(
163	            message=f"Unknown job type {job_type!r}",
164	            code="jobs.unknown_job_type",
165	        )
166	    job = Job(
167	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
168	        job_type=job_type,
169	        payload=payload,
170	        submitted_by_user_id=submitted_by,
171	    )
172	    session.add(job)
173	    await session.flush()
174	    return job
175	
176	
177	# --- Scheduler seam ----------------------------------------------------------------
178	
179	
180	@runtime_checkable
181	class JobScheduler(Protocol):
182	    """The swappable contract (module docstring): schedule ``job_id`` for execution after its
183	    PENDING row is committed. The in-process implementation needs the submitter's session
184	    factory to reach the same database; a queue-backed implementation enqueues the id and
185	    ignores it (workers own their engine)."""
186	
187	    def schedule(
188	        self, job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
189	    ) -> None: ...
190	
191	
192	# Live in-process tasks, kept so they are not garbage-collected mid-run; each discards itself
193	# on completion. ``wait_for_jobs`` (tests) awaits the current loop's members.
194	_live_tasks: set[asyncio.Task[None]] = set()
195	
196	# Per-event-loop semaphores: asyncio primitives bind to the first loop that awaits them and
197	# raise if reused on another, and the test suite runs one loop per test — so the cap is created
198	# lazily per loop (weak keys: a finished test's loop drops its entry).
199	_semaphores: weakref.WeakKeyDictionary[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, asyncio.Semaphore] = (
200	    weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()
201	)
202	
203	
204	def _semaphore() -> asyncio.Semaphore:
205	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
206	    semaphore = _semaphores.get(loop)
207	    if semaphore is None:
208	        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS)
209	        _semaphores[loop] = semaphore
210	    return semaphore
211	
212	
213	class InProcessJobScheduler:
214	    """v1 execution: an asyncio task on the running loop (the request's loop), capped by the
215	    per-loop semaphore. Scheduled post-commit by contract, so the PENDING row is visible."""
216	
217	    def schedule(
218	        self, job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
219	    ) -> None:
220	        for task in list(_live_tasks):  # hygiene: drop tasks whose loop is gone (test teardown)
221	            if task.get_loop().is_closed():
222	                _live_tasks.discard(task)
223	        task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(_execute_job(job_id, session_factory))
224	        _live_tasks.add(task)
225	        task.add_done_callback(_live_tasks.discard)
226	
227	
228	# Module singleton, same pattern as the D-011 event bus: a queue-backed scheduler replaces THIS
229	# binding and nothing else moves.
230	scheduler: JobScheduler = InProcessJobScheduler()
231	
232	
233	def schedule_job(
234	    job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
235	) -> None:
236	    """Schedule a committed PENDING job via the active scheduler. Call strictly AFTER the
237	    submitting ``run_in_uow`` has committed."""
238	    scheduler.schedule(job_id, session_factory)
239	
240	
241	async def wait_for_jobs() -> None:
242	    """Test helper: await every live in-process job task on the CURRENT loop (including tasks
243	    those jobs schedule while we wait), so assertions after submit are deterministic. A task
244	    raising here is a runner bug — ``_execute_job`` converts handler failures to FAILED rows."""
245	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
246	    while True:
247	        pending = [t for t in _live_tasks if t.get_loop() is loop and not t.done()]
248	        if not pending:
249	            return
250	        await asyncio.gather(*pending)
251	
252	
253	# --- Runner -------------------------------------------------------------------------
254	
255	
256	async def _execute_job(
257	    job_id: uuid.UUID, session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
258	) -> None:
259	    """Execute one job in its own session/transaction (module docstring: context restore, the
260	    RUNNING commit, run_in_uow for the handler + COMPLETED, FAILED on exception)."""
261	    async with _semaphore(), session_factory() as session:
262	        # The job's tenant is unknown until the row is read — load under system_context
263	        # (the D-007 fail-closed filter would otherwise reject the read).
264	        with system_context():
265	            job = await session.get(Job, job_id)
266	        if job is None:
267	            logger.error("Scheduled job %s not found; scheduled before commit?", job_id)
268	            return
269	        actor_token = actor_user_id_ctx.set(job.submitted_by_user_id)
270	        try:
271	            with tenant_context(job.tenant_id):
272	                await _run_handler(session, job)
273	        finally:
274	            actor_user_id_ctx.reset(actor_token)
275	
276	
277	async def _run_handler(session: AsyncSession, job: Job) -> None:
278	    """RUNNING (own commit) -> handler inside run_in_uow with COMPLETED set in the same uow
279	    (business writes + terminal status commit atomically) -> on ANY exception the uow has
280	    rolled the work back; commit only the FAILED status + truncated error."""
281	    # Plain locals: a rollback below expires the instance, and expired-attribute access on an
282	    # async session raises (MissingGreenlet) — never touch job.<col> in the except path.
283	    tenant_id, job_pk, job_type = job.tenant_id, job.id, job.job_type
284	    job.status = JobStatus.RUNNING.value
285	    job.started_at = datetime.now(UTC)
286	    await session.commit()
287	
288	    handler = _registry.get(job_type)
289	    try:
290	        if handler is None:
291	            # Validated at submit; only reachable if the code shipped between submit and run.
292	            raise ValidationFailedError(
293	                message=f"Unknown job type {job_type!r}",
294	                code="jobs.unknown_job_type",
295	            )
296	
297	        async def work() -> None:
298	            result = await handler(session, tenant_id, dict(job.payload or {}))
299	            job.status = JobStatus.COMPLETED.value
300	            job.result = result
301	            job.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
302	
303	        await run_in_uow(session, work)
304	    except Exception as exc:
305	        logger.exception("Background job %s (%s) failed", job_pk, job_type)
306	        # run_in_uow rolled back and expired the instance; reload it before writing the
307	        # terminal status (its row is still RUNNING from the pre-handler commit).
308	        await session.refresh(job)
309	        job.status = JobStatus.FAILED.value
310	        job.error = (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__)[:_ERROR_MAX_CHARS]
311	        job.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
312	        await session.commit()
313	
314

4	Inventory OWNS reorder_point/reorder_quantity on the item (5.1) and exposes
5	``items_below_reorder_point`` (a set-based query, no N+1); the DRAFT requisition is a PROCUREMENT
6	document (6.2). So this scan reads the inventory query downward (STRUCTURE §5 — never imports
7	inventory models/service), then creates ONE requisition with a line per below-reorder item
8	(quantity = reorder_quantity, in the item's base UoM) via the existing 6.2 requisition create — so
9	the proposal flows through the normal requisition approval chain.
10	
11	IDEMPOTENT dedup: a second scan the same day must not duplicate an open draft requisition line for
12	an item already proposed. ``open_requisition_item_ids`` collects the item ids already on any
13	DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED (un-converted) requisition line; the scan SKIPS those items. So re-running
14	the scan only adds genuinely new shortfalls. Returns the created requisition, or None when nothing
15	needs reordering (the endpoint maps None to a 200 "nothing to reorder").
16	
17	PERFORMANCE §3: the scan is INLINE (a tenant's item count is modest in v1 and the work is two
18	set-based queries + one requisition insert). A per-tenant volume that outgrows the sync budget would
19	move it behind the existing job runner ('procurement.reorder_scan') — documented, not built for v1.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import uuid
25	
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	
29	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
30	from app.modules.procurement.constants import RequisitionStatus
31	from app.modules.procurement.models import PurchaseRequisition, PurchaseRequisitionLine
32	from app.modules.procurement.schemas import RequisitionCreate, RequisitionLineCreate
33	from app.modules.procurement.service.requisitions import create_requisition
34	
35	# A requisition line is still OPEN (its item should not be re-proposed) while the requisition is in
36	# any of these states — it has not been CONVERTED to a PO/RFQ, REJECTED or CANCELLED yet.
37	_OPEN_REQUISITION_STATUSES = (
38	    RequisitionStatus.DRAFT.value,
39	    RequisitionStatus.SUBMITTED.value,
40	    RequisitionStatus.APPROVED.value,
41	)
42	
43	
44	async def open_requisition_item_ids(
45	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
46	) -> set[uuid.UUID]:
47	    """The item ids already on an open (un-converted) requisition line (PLAN 6.4). The dedup guard:
48	    the reorder scan skips these so a re-run does not duplicate a still-open proposal. ONE set-based
49	    query joining lines to their open requisitions (no per-item N+1, PERFORMANCE §2)."""
50	    stmt = (
51	        select(PurchaseRequisitionLine.item_id)
52	        .join(
53	            PurchaseRequisition,
54	            (PurchaseRequisitionLine.tenant_id == PurchaseRequisition.tenant_id)
55	            & (PurchaseRequisitionLine.requisition_id == PurchaseRequisition.id),
56	        )
57	        .where(
58	            PurchaseRequisition.tenant_id == tenant_id,
59	            PurchaseRequisition.status.in_(_OPEN_REQUISITION_STATUSES),
60	        )
61	    )
62	    return {row[0] for row in (await session.execute(stmt)).all()}
63	
64	
65	async def run_reorder_scan(
66	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, *, requested_by: uuid.UUID | None = None
67	) -> PurchaseRequisition | None:
68	    """Scan for below-reorder items and raise a DRAFT requisition proposing replenishment (PLAN 6.4,
69	    D-042). Reads ``items_below_reorder_point`` (inventory, downward), skips items already on an
70	    open requisition line (the idempotent dedup), resolves each item's base UoM + a default
71	    currency, and
72	    creates ONE requisition with a line per remaining item (quantity = reorder_quantity) via the
73	    existing 6.2 create — so it flows through the normal approval chain. Returns the requisition, or
74	    None when nothing needs reordering (no shortfalls, or all already proposed)."""
75	    below = await inventory_queries.items_below_reorder_point(session, tenant_id)
76	    if not below:
77	        return None
78	    already_open = await open_requisition_item_ids(session, tenant_id)
79	    to_order = [(item_id, qty) for (item_id, _oh, _rp, qty) in below if item_id not in already_open]
80	    if not to_order:
81	        return None
82	
83	    currency_code = await _default_currency(session, tenant_id)
84	    lines: list[RequisitionLineCreate] = []
85	    for item_id, reorder_quantity in to_order:
86	        base_uom_id = await inventory_queries.get_base_uom(session, tenant_id, item_id)
87	        if base_uom_id is None:
88	            continue
89	        lines.append(
90	            RequisitionLineCreate(
91	                item_id=item_id,
92	                description="Reorder-point replenishment",
93	                quantity=reorder_quantity,
94	                uom_id=base_uom_id,
95	                currency_code=currency_code,
96	            )
97	        )
98	    if not lines:
99	        return None
100	    return await create_requisition(
101	        session,
102	        tenant_id,
103	        RequisitionCreate(
104	            requested_by=requested_by, notes="Auto-generated reorder scan", lines=lines
105	        ),
106	    )
107	
108	
109	async def _default_currency(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> str:
110	    """The currency code the reorder requisition lines carry (PLAN 6.4): the tenant's functional
111	    currency (the reporting currency, the natural default for an internal replenishment estimate
112	    with no vendor yet). Reads finance/queries downward; falls back to USD when unconfigured (the
113	    same single-currency default the costing path uses)."""
114	    from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
115	
116	    return await finance_queries.functional_currency_or_none(session, tenant_id) or "USD"

1	"""The depreciation run engine (PLAN 4.10): per-period computation + the posting run.
2	
3	**compute_depreciation** is the pure per-asset/per-period formula. ``period_index`` is the
4	asset's 1-based position in ITS OWN schedule (prior entry count + 1 — depreciation periods,
5	not calendar months), ``prior_accumulated`` the sum of its prior entries:
6	
7	- STRAIGHT_LINE: drift-free cumulative formulation — amount(n) =
8	  quantize((cost - salvage) x n / life) - prior_accumulated, and the FINAL period (n >= life)
9	  takes exactly (cost - salvage) - prior_accumulated, so the schedule sums to cost - salvage
10	  EXACTLY (largest-remainder-style: per-period rounding can never drift because each period is
11	  cumulative-to-date minus what was already taken).
12	- DECLINING_BALANCE: amount(n) = quantize(NBV_start x annual_rate / 12), floored so NBV never
13	  crosses salvage (the crossing period takes NBV_start - salvage and lands EXACTLY on salvage);
14	  when the schedule exhausts (n >= life) the remainder to salvage is taken.
15	
16	**run_depreciation** is set-based (PERFORMANCE §2): eligible ACTIVE assets are selected with a
17	NOT EXISTS anti-join on fin_depreciation_entries (an asset depreciates once per period — the
18	UNIQUE(tenant, asset, period) backbone makes overlapping runs collide at the DB); prior
19	accumulated amounts come from ONE grouped aggregate (no per-asset N+1); the entries are written
20	with ONE bulk executemany insert; and the run posts ONE journal entry with lines GROUPED per
21	(expense account, cost centre) on the debit side and per accumulated-depreciation account on
22	the credit side (document_type DEPRECIATION). Assets reaching cost - salvage flip
23	FULLY_DEPRECIATED. A re-run for a fully-depreciated period finds nothing eligible and returns
24	the existing POSTED run unchanged (the allocation-run idempotency pattern); the HTTP endpoint
25	is additionally Idempotent (D-013). Runs above DEPRECIATION_RUN_SYNC_MAX_ASSETS execute as a
26	``finance.depreciation_run`` background job (PERFORMANCE §3).
27	
28	Reads + the asset-register projection live in ``service/depreciation_read.py`` (STRUCTURE
29	§8.4 split, the journal.py/journal_read.py precedent).
30	"""
31	
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import uuid
35	from datetime import date
36	from decimal import Decimal
37	from typing import Any
38	
39	from sqlalchemy import func, insert, select
40	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
41	
42	from app.core import docflow
43	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
44	from app.core.jobs import register_job
45	from app.core.money import currency_decimals, quantize_money
46	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
47	from app.modules.finance.constants import (
48	    DEPRECIATION_NUMBER_PADDING,
49	    DEPRECIATION_NUMBER_PREFIX,
50	    DEPRECIATION_POSTS_LINK,
51	    DEPRECIATION_RUN_DOC_TYPE,
52	    DEPRECIATION_RUN_JOB,
53	    DEPRECIATION_SEQUENCE_NAME,
54	    AssetStatus,
55	    DepreciationMethod,
56	    DepreciationRunStatus,
57	    DocumentType,
58	    PeriodStatus,
59	)
60	from app.modules.finance.models import Asset, DepreciationEntry, DepreciationRun, FiscalPeriod
61	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate, JournalLineCreate
62	from app.modules.finance.service.depreciation_read import existing_posted_run
63	from app.modules.finance.service.journal import create_draft_entry, post_entry

65	
66	def compute_depreciation(
67	    asset: Asset, period_index: int, prior_accumulated: Decimal
68	) -> Decimal:
69	    """The per-period charge for ``asset`` at schedule position ``period_index`` (module
70	    docstring). Pure; quantized to the asset currency's minor unit; never negative and never
71	    takes NBV below salvage."""
72	    places = currency_decimals(asset.currency_code)
73	    cost = Decimal(str(asset.acquisition_cost))
74	    salvage = Decimal(str(asset.salvage_value))
75	    depreciable = cost - salvage
76	    if depreciable <= 0 or prior_accumulated >= depreciable:
77	        return Decimal(0)
78	
79	    if asset.depreciation_method == DepreciationMethod.STRAIGHT_LINE.value:
80	        if period_index >= asset.useful_life_months:
81	            return depreciable - prior_accumulated
82	        cumulative = quantize_money(
83	            depreciable * period_index / asset.useful_life_months, places
84	        )
85	        return max(cumulative - prior_accumulated, Decimal(0))
86	
87	    # DECLINING_BALANCE: NBV_start x (annual rate / 12), floored at salvage.
88	    nbv_start = cost - prior_accumulated
89	    if period_index >= asset.useful_life_months:
90	        return nbv_start - salvage
91	    annual_rate = Decimal(str(asset.declining_rate_percent)) / Decimal(100)
92	    amount = quantize_money(nbv_start * annual_rate / Decimal(12), places)
93	    if nbv_start - amount < salvage:
94	        amount = nbv_start - salvage
95	    return max(amount, Decimal(0))
96	
97	
98	def _eligible_assets_stmt(tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID):
99	    """ACTIVE assets NOT yet depreciated for ``period_id`` — the set-based anti-join."""
100	    already = select(DepreciationEntry.id).where(
101	        DepreciationEntry.tenant_id == tenant_id,
102	        DepreciationEntry.asset_id == Asset.id,
103	        DepreciationEntry.fiscal_period_id == period_id,
104	    )
105	    return select(Asset).where(
106	        Asset.tenant_id == tenant_id,
107	        Asset.status == AssetStatus.ACTIVE.value,
108	        ~already.exists(),
109	    )
110	
111	
112	async def count_eligible_assets(
113	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID
114	) -> int:
115	    """How many assets a run for ``period_id`` would touch — the router's sync/background
116	    threshold probe (PERFORMANCE §3), one COUNT query."""
117	    stmt = select(func.count()).select_from(
118	        _eligible_assets_stmt(tenant_id, period_id).subquery()
119	    )
120	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()
121	
122	
123	async def _require_open_period(
124	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID, run_date: date
125	) -> FiscalPeriod:
126	    """The target period must exist, be OPEN (service half of D-018; the journal's period
127	    trigger is the bypass-proof backstop) and contain ``run_date`` (the posted entry's date —
128	    the trigger re-derives the period from it, so a mismatch would post elsewhere)."""
129	    period = await session.get(FiscalPeriod, period_id)
130	    if period is None or period.tenant_id != tenant_id:
131	        raise ValidationFailedError(
132	            message="The fiscal period does not exist in this tenant",
133	            code="finance.depreciation_period_not_found",
134	            details={"fiscal_period_id": str(period_id)},
135	        )
136	    if period.status != PeriodStatus.OPEN.value:
137	        raise ValidationFailedError(
138	            message="Depreciation cannot post into a closed period",
139	            code="finance.period_closed",
140	            details={"fiscal_period_id": str(period_id)},
141	        )
142	    if not period.start_date <= run_date <= period.end_date:
143	        raise ValidationFailedError(
144	            message="run_date must fall inside the fiscal period being depreciated",
145	            code="finance.depreciation_run_date_outside_period",
146	            details={"run_date": run_date.isoformat()},
147	        )
148	    return period
149	
150	
151	def _grouped_lines(
152	    debits: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID | None], Decimal],
153	    credits: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal],
154	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
155	    """One compact entry: Dr per (expense account, cost centre), Cr per accumulated account —
156	    aggregated, never per-asset lines. Sorted for deterministic line numbering."""
157	    lines = [
158	        JournalLineCreate(
159	            account_id=account_id,
160	            description="Depreciation expense",
161	            transaction_debit_amount=amount,
162	            cost_center_id=cost_center_id,
163	        )
164	        for (account_id, cost_center_id), amount in sorted(
165	            debits.items(), key=lambda kv: (str(kv[0][0]), str(kv[0][1] or ""))
166	        )
167	    ]
168	    lines.extend(
169	        JournalLineCreate(
170	            account_id=account_id,
171	            description="Accumulated depreciation",
172	            transaction_credit_amount=amount,
173	        )
174	        for account_id, amount in sorted(credits.items(), key=lambda kv: str(kv[0]))
175	    )
176	    return lines
177	
178	
179	async def _nothing_to_depreciate(
180	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period_id: uuid.UUID
181	) -> DepreciationRun:
182	    """Nothing eligible: return the period's existing POSTED run unchanged (idempotent
183	    re-run, the allocation pattern) or raise a clear 422 when the period never ran."""
184	    existing = await existing_posted_run(session, tenant_id, period_id)
185	    if existing is not None:
186	        return existing
187	    raise ValidationFailedError(
188	        message="No active assets to depreciate for this period",
189	        code="finance.depreciation_nothing_to_depreciate",
190	        details={"fiscal_period_id": str(period_id)},
191	    )
192	
193	
194	async def run_depreciation(
195	    session: AsyncSession,
196	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
197	    period_id: uuid.UUID,
198	    run_date: date,
199	) -> DepreciationRun:
200	    """Depreciate every eligible ACTIVE asset for one period (module docstring). The SQL
201	    statement count is CONSTANT in the asset count (selection, ONE grouped prior aggregate,
202	    ONE bulk entry insert, one grouped journal entry, run bookkeeping) plus one status write
203	    per asset that flips FULLY_DEPRECIATED. Caller commits via uow (D-011)."""
204	    period = await _require_open_period(session, tenant_id, period_id, run_date)
205	    assets = list(
206	        (
207	            await session.execute(
208	                _eligible_assets_stmt(tenant_id, period_id).order_by(Asset.asset_number)
209	            )
210	        )
211	        .scalars()
212	        .all()
213	    )
214	    if not assets:
215	        return await _nothing_to_depreciate(session, tenant_id, period_id)
216	    currencies = {asset.currency_code for asset in assets}
217	    if len(currencies) > 1:
218	        raise ValidationFailedError(
219	            message="All assets in a depreciation run must share one currency",
220	            code="finance.depreciation_mixed_currencies",
221	            details={"currencies": sorted(currencies)},
222	        )
223	    currency_code = assets[0].currency_code
224	
225	    # Prior schedule position + accumulated per asset, in ONE grouped query (no N+1).
226	    prior_rows = (
227	        await session.execute(
228	            select(
229	                DepreciationEntry.asset_id,
230	                func.count(DepreciationEntry.id),
231	                func.coalesce(func.sum(DepreciationEntry.amount), 0),
232	            )
233	            .where(
234	                DepreciationEntry.tenant_id == tenant_id,
235	                DepreciationEntry.asset_id.in_([asset.id for asset in assets]),
236	            )
237	            .group_by(DepreciationEntry.asset_id)
238	        )
239	    ).all()
240	    prior = {asset_id: (count, Decimal(str(total))) for asset_id, count, total in prior_rows}
241	
242	    entry_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
243	    debits: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID | None], Decimal] = {}
244	    credits: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
245	    flipped: list[Asset] = []
246	    total = Decimal(0)
247	    for asset in assets:
248	        prior_count, prior_accumulated = prior.get(asset.id, (0, Decimal(0)))
249	        amount = compute_depreciation(asset, prior_count + 1, prior_accumulated)
250	        if amount <= 0:  # nothing this period; the asset stays eligible for later runs
251	            continue
252	        accumulated_after = prior_accumulated + amount
253	        nbv_after = Decimal(str(asset.acquisition_cost)) - accumulated_after
254	        entry_rows.append(
255	            {
256	                "id": uuid.uuid4(),
257	                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
258	                "asset_id": asset.id,
259	                "fiscal_period_id": period_id,
260	                "amount": amount,
261	                "accumulated_after": accumulated_after,
262	                "nbv_after": nbv_after,
263	            }
264	        )
265	        debit_key = (asset.depreciation_expense_account_id, asset.cost_center_id)
266	        debits[debit_key] = debits.get(debit_key, Decimal(0)) + amount
267	        credit_key = asset.accumulated_depreciation_account_id
268	        credits[credit_key] = credits.get(credit_key, Decimal(0)) + amount
269	        total += amount
270	        if nbv_after == Decimal(str(asset.salvage_value)):
271	            flipped.append(asset)
272	
273	    if not entry_rows:
274	        return await _nothing_to_depreciate(session, tenant_id, period_id)
275	
276	    # ONE grouped journal entry for the whole run (Dr expense / Cr accumulated).
277	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
278	        session,
279	        tenant_id,
280	        JournalEntryCreate(
281	            posting_date=run_date,
282	            currency_code=currency_code,
283	            description=f"Depreciation {period.name}",
284	            document_type=DocumentType.DEPRECIATION,
285	            lines=_grouped_lines(debits, credits),
286	        ),
287	    )
288	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, entry.id)
289	
290	    run = await _track_run(
291	        session, tenant_id, period_id, run_date, entry.id, total, len(entry_rows)
292	    )
293	    # The PERFORMANCE §2 bulk insert: one ORM-enabled executemany, explicit tenant_id per row.
294	    # The UNIQUE(tenant, asset, period) backbone rejects any overlapping run here.
295	    await session.execute(
296	        insert(DepreciationEntry), [{**row, "run_id": run.id} for row in entry_rows]
297	    )
298	    await docflow.link_documents(
299	        session,
300	        tenant_id,
301	        predecessor=run.document_id,
302	        successor=entry.document_id,
303	        link_type=DEPRECIATION_POSTS_LINK,
304	    )
305	
306	    # Loaded-object status flips (audited, D-010); registry status follows.
307	    for asset in flipped:
308	        asset.status = AssetStatus.FULLY_DEPRECIATED.value
309	        await docflow.set_document_status(
310	            session, tenant_id, asset.document_id, status=AssetStatus.FULLY_DEPRECIATED.value
311	        )
312	    await session.flush()
313	    return run
314	
315	
316	async def _track_run(
317	    session: AsyncSession,
318	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
319	    period_id: uuid.UUID,
320	    run_date: date,
321	    journal_entry_id: uuid.UUID,
322	    total_amount: Decimal,
323	    asset_count: int,
324	) -> DepreciationRun:
325	    """Register the run document, claim its gapless DEP number, persist the run row (D-012)."""
326	    run_id = uuid.uuid4()
327	    document = await docflow.register_document(
328	        session,
329	        tenant_id,
330	        DEPRECIATION_RUN_DOC_TYPE,
331	        run_id,
332	        doc_number=None,
333	        status=DepreciationRunStatus.POSTED.value,
334	    )
335	    await ensure_sequence(
336	        session,
337	        tenant_id,
338	        DEPRECIATION_SEQUENCE_NAME,
339	        DEPRECIATION_NUMBER_PREFIX,
340	        DEPRECIATION_NUMBER_PADDING,
341	        year_reset=True,
342	    )
343	    run_number = await claim_number(
344	        session, tenant_id, DEPRECIATION_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=run_date
345	    )
346	    run = DepreciationRun(
347	        id=run_id,
348	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
349	        document_id=document.id,
350	        fiscal_period_id=period_id,
351	        run_number=run_number,
352	        run_date=run_date,
353	        status=DepreciationRunStatus.POSTED.value,
354	        journal_entry_id=journal_entry_id,
355	        total_amount=total_amount,
356	        asset_count=asset_count,
357	    )
358	    session.add(run)
359	    await session.flush()
360	    await docflow.set_document_status(
361	        session,
362	        tenant_id,
363	        document.id,
364	        status=DepreciationRunStatus.POSTED.value,
365	        doc_number=run_number,
366	    )
367	    return run
368	
369	
370	@register_job(DEPRECIATION_RUN_JOB)
371	async def depreciation_run_job(
372	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: dict[str, Any]
373	) -> dict[str, Any]:
374	    """Background-job handler (PERFORMANCE §3): a run over >100 assets executes as a job and
375	    the endpoint returns 202 {job_id}. Delegates to :func:`run_depreciation`."""
376	    run = await run_depreciation(
377	        session,
378	        tenant_id,
379	        uuid.UUID(payload["fiscal_period_id"]),
380	        date.fromisoformat(payload["run_date"]),
381	    )
382	    await session.refresh(run)
383	    return {
384	        "run_id": str(run.id),
385	        "run_number": run.run_number,
386	        "journal_entry_id": str(run.journal_entry_id),
387	        "asset_count": run.asset_count,
388	        "total_amount": str(run.total_amount),
389	    }

1	"""Manufacturing's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Manufacturing sits above inventory/procurement/sales in the dependency order. PLAN 8.2 (production
4	orders) and 8.3 (MRP + rough capacity) read THIS file to resolve an item's active BOM/routing and a
5	work centre's capacity; it is the ONLY manufacturing file those flows import. Keep it thin and
6	stable — it is a contract.

8	The "active" resolvers return the ACTIVE + ``is_default`` version of a BOM/routing for an item (the
9	one the service guarantees is unique per item). ``bom_components`` / ``routing_operations`` return
10	the lines an exploder/scheduler walks. Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under
11	the caller's tenant context, so the D-007 filter applies on top — ordinary tenant-scoped reads.
12	"""
13	
14	import uuid
15	from decimal import Decimal
16	
17	from sqlalchemy import select
18	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
19	
20	from app.modules.manufacturing.constants import (
21	    BomStatus,
22	    ProductionOrderStatus,
23	    RoutingStatus,

1	"""Sales' cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Sales sits above inventory and finance in the dependency order: the O2C documents in 7.2–7.4
4	(quote → order → delivery → invoice) and finance AR reporting read THIS file to resolve customer
5	state + prices synchronously; sales imports finance/queries + inventory/queries downward. Keep this
6	surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is the ONLY sales file other modules import.
7	
8	The central D-029 link: finance AR stores a customer on each invoice/receipt as an opaque
9	``partner_id`` (no FK). ``get_customer_for_partner`` resolves that ``partner_id`` back to a
10	``Customer`` so AR aging / reporting can render the customer's name and payment terms — the
11	``partner_id`` IS the ``Customer.id``, so it is a thin alias over ``get_customer`` named for the
12	reporting intent (the exact mirror of procurement's ``get_vendor_for_partner``).
13	
14	The PRICE RESOLVER is exposed too: ``resolve_price`` (the public entry 7.2 prices lines through)
15	delegates to ``service/price_resolution.resolve_price`` (the best-match picker, D-043), keeping the
16	rule that other modules import only this file.
17	
18	The ORDER reads 7.3/7.4 call — ``get_sales_order``, ``get_order_for_delivery`` /
19	``get_order_for_invoice``, the per-line open-quantity helpers ``so_line_open_to_deliver`` /
20	``_to_invoice`` / ``_to_return`` (ordered/delivered/invoiced minus the next stage), and the ATP +
21	credit helpers the confirm gate uses (``committed_quantity``, ``atp_check``,
22	``open_confirmed_order_value``, ``customer_open_ar``) — the last two making SANCTIONED downward
23	cross-module reads (inventory on-hand, procurement on-order, finance open AR).
24	
25	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
26	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
27	"""

259	# --- ATP: committed quantity + the availability check (PLAN 7.2, D-044) -----------------------
260	
261	
262	async def committed_quantity(
263	    session: AsyncSession,
264	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
265	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
266	    *,
267	    exclude_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
268	) -> Decimal:
269	    """The quantity of an item COMMITTED by confirmed-but-undelivered sales orders (PLAN 7.2, D-044)
270	    — the reservation an ATP scan subtracts from on-hand. Sums ``ordered − delivered`` over order
271	    lines for ``item_id`` on CONFIRMED / PARTIALLY_DELIVERED orders (a CONFIRMED order has reserved
272	    its undelivered quantity; a DRAFT / CREDIT_BLOCKED / CANCELLED / fully-DELIVERED / INVOICED /
273	    CLOSED order commits nothing). ``exclude_order_id`` drops one order from the sum — used when
274	    confirming so an order's own demand is checked against availability NET of other commitments.
275	    SET-BASED (no per-order N+1, PERFORMANCE §2): one filtered join, summed in PYTHON over the small
276	    open set so the exact-decimal QuantityType round-trips identically on both engines (D-015)."""
277	    stmt = (
278	        select(SalesOrderLine.ordered_quantity, SalesOrderLine.delivered_quantity)
279	        .join(
280	            SalesOrder,
281	            (SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == SalesOrder.tenant_id)
282	            & (SalesOrderLine.order_id == SalesOrder.id),
283	        )
284	        .where(
285	            SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
286	            SalesOrderLine.item_id == item_id,
287	            SalesOrder.status.in_(
288	                [
289	                    SalesOrderStatus.CONFIRMED.value,
290	                    SalesOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_DELIVERED.value,
291	                ]
292	            ),
293	            SalesOrderLine.delivered_quantity < SalesOrderLine.ordered_quantity,
294	        )
295	    )
296	    if exclude_order_id is not None:
297	        stmt = stmt.where(SalesOrder.id != exclude_order_id)
298	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
299	    return sum(
300	        (Decimal(str(ordered)) - Decimal(str(delivered)) for ordered, delivered in rows),
301	        Decimal(0),
302	    )

305	@dataclass(frozen=True)
306	class AtpResult:
307	    """The ATP outcome for one item (D-044): ``available`` = on_hand − committed + on_order;
308	    ``atp_ok`` is ``available >= requested``; ``shortfall`` is ``requested − available`` clamped at
309	    0. Informational — a shortfall flags a backorder, it does NOT block confirmation."""
310	
311	    item_id: uuid.UUID
312	    requested_quantity: Decimal
313	    on_hand: Decimal
314	    committed: Decimal
315	    on_order: Decimal
316	    available: Decimal
317	    atp_ok: bool
318	    shortfall: Decimal
319

321	async def atp_check(
322	    session: AsyncSession,
323	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
324	    *,
325	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
326	    quantity: Decimal,
327	    on_date: date,
328	    exclude_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
329	) -> AtpResult:
330	    """Available-to-promise for one item (PLAN 7.2, D-044): availability = inventory on-hand −
331	    committed (confirmed-undelivered sales orders) + on-order (procurement open-incoming). The
332	    ``on_date`` is the wire contract (v1 is a point-in-time snapshot; date-phased ATP is a later).
333	    Three bounded cross-module reads, no N+1. ``exclude_order_id`` excludes one order from the
334	    committed sum (confirm checks an order net of OTHER commitments)."""
335	    requested = Decimal(str(quantity))
336	    on_hand = Decimal(str(await inventory_queries.total_on_hand(session, tenant_id, item_id)))
337	    committed = await committed_quantity(
338	        session, tenant_id, item_id, exclude_order_id=exclude_order_id
339	    )
340	    on_order = Decimal(
341	        str(await procurement_queries.open_incoming_quantity(session, tenant_id, item_id))
342	    )
343	    available = on_hand - committed + on_order
344	    shortfall = requested - available
345	    if shortfall < 0:
346	        shortfall = Decimal(0)
347	    return AtpResult(
348	        item_id=item_id,
349	        requested_quantity=requested,
350	        on_hand=on_hand,
351	        committed=committed,
352	        on_order=on_order,
353	        available=available,
354	        atp_ok=available >= requested,
355	        shortfall=shortfall,
356	    )
357	
358	
359	# --- Credit exposure (PLAN 7.2, D-044) --------------------------------------------------------
360	
361	
362	async def open_confirmed_order_value(
363	    session: AsyncSession,
364	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
365	    customer_id: uuid.UUID,
366	    *,
367	    exclude_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
368	) -> Decimal:
369	    """The total value of a customer's OPEN confirmed orders not yet billed (PLAN 7.2, D-044) — the
370	    open-order side of credit exposure. Sums ``total_amount`` over the customer's CONFIRMED /
371	    PARTIALLY_DELIVERED / DELIVERED orders (committed but not fully invoiced; an INVOICED order's
372	    exposure has moved to AR, a CLOSED/CANCELLED/DRAFT/CREDIT_BLOCKED order is nothing).
373	    ``exclude_order_id`` drops one order (the one being confirmed). SET-BASED (no N+1): a scan on
374	    the (tenant, customer_id, status) index, summed in Python for exact MoneyType (D-015)."""
375	    stmt = select(SalesOrder.total_amount).where(
376	        SalesOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
377	        SalesOrder.customer_id == customer_id,
378	        SalesOrder.status.in_(
379	            [
380	                SalesOrderStatus.CONFIRMED.value,
381	                SalesOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_DELIVERED.value,
382	                SalesOrderStatus.DELIVERED.value,
383	            ]
384	        ),
385	    )
386	    if exclude_order_id is not None:
387	        stmt = stmt.where(SalesOrder.id != exclude_order_id)
388	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
389	    return sum((Decimal(str(value)) for (value,) in rows), Decimal(0))
390	
391	
392	async def customer_open_ar(
393	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
394	) -> Decimal:
395	    """The customer's open AR (sum of open_amount on POSTED customer invoices) — the receivables
396	    side of credit exposure (PLAN 7.2, D-044). A thin alias over finance's ``customer_open_balance``
397	    keyed by the opaque partner_id (= Customer.id, D-029), named for the credit-check intent so the
398	    order flow reads it without importing finance models (the bottom-up cross-module read)."""
399	    return await finance_queries.customer_open_balance(session, tenant_id, customer_id)

1	"""Inventory's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Inventory sits just above finance in the dependency order: every module above it (procurement,
4	sales, manufacturing) may import THIS file to read inventory state synchronously, and inventory
5	imports only finance/queries downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is
6	the ONLY inventory file other modules import.
7	
8	For PLAN 5.1 it exposes the item-master reads those modules will need: existence checks, the
9	item's base UoM and costing method, and the category's GL-account wiring (so the COGS handler can
10	resolve where to post when stock issues land in 5.2+). PLAN 5.2 adds the ON-HAND projection reads
11	(``total_on_hand``, ``on_hand_by_bin``, ``on_hand_by_lot``) — what sales ATP and procurement will
12	call: they read the MAINTAINED ``inv_stock_quants`` projection (D-036), an indexed aggregate, never
13	an unbounded SUM over the move history (PERFORMANCE §1).
14	
15	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
16	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
17	"""
18	
19	import uuid
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	
22	from sqlalchemy import func, select
23	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
24	
25	from app.modules.inventory.constants import CostingMethod
26	from app.modules.inventory.models import (
27	    Bin,
28	    CostLayer,
29	    Item,
30	    ItemCategory,

39	async def get_item(
40	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
41	) -> Item | None:
42	    """The item with ``item_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets another module read an item's master
43	    fields (name, type, base UoM, costing method) without importing inventory models directly."""
44	    stmt = select(Item).where(Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id)
45	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

48	async def item_exists(
49	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
50	) -> bool:
51	    """Whether an item with ``item_id`` exists in the tenant. The cheap existence check a sales or
52	    procurement line uses to validate its item_id dimension (the inventory analogue of finance's
53	    ``account_exists_by_id``)."""
54	    stmt = select(Item.id).where(Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id)
55	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None

58	async def uom_exists(
59	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, uom_id: uuid.UUID
60	) -> bool:
61	    """Whether a unit of measure with ``uom_id`` exists in the tenant. The UoM analogue of
62	    ``item_exists``: a manufacturing BOM header/component references the parent/component UoM by
63	    opaque id (D-029) and validates it through this contract before writing — UoMs and items are
64	    distinct inventory entities, so this cannot be folded into ``item_exists``."""
65	    stmt = select(Uom.id).where(Uom.tenant_id == tenant_id, Uom.id == uom_id)
66	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
67
