69	async def get_costing_method(
70	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
71	) -> CostingMethod | None:
72	    """The item's costing method (D-020), or None if the item does not exist. The costing engine
73	    (5.3) reads this to choose moving-average vs FIFO; exposed so other modules can too."""
74	    stmt = select(Item.costing_method).where(
75	        Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id
76	    )
77	    value = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
78	    return CostingMethod(value) if value is not None else None
79	
80	
81	async def get_base_uom(
82	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
83	) -> uuid.UUID | None:
84	    """The item's base UoM id (the unit it is stored/costed in), or None if the item does not
85	    exist. A document line in another UoM converts to this base via ``service.convert_quantity``."""
86	    stmt = select(Item.base_uom_id).where(
87	        Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id
88	    )
89	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
90	
91	
92	async def get_category_accounts(
93	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
94	) -> tuple[uuid.UUID | None, uuid.UUID | None, uuid.UUID | None] | None:
95	    """The GL-account wiring (inventory, COGS, price-difference) of an item's category (D-020),
96	    or None if the item does not exist. The COGS handler (5.2+) resolves where to post a goods
97	    issue from this tuple. Any element may be None when the category has not wired that account
98	    yet — the issuing flow validates presence before it posts. One join, item -> category."""
99	    stmt = (
100	        select(
101	            ItemCategory.inventory_account_id,
102	            ItemCategory.cogs_account_id,
103	            ItemCategory.price_difference_account_id,
104	        )
105	        .join(Item, Item.category_id == ItemCategory.id)
106	        .where(Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id)
107	    )
108	    row = (await session.execute(stmt)).first()
109	    return (row[0], row[1], row[2]) if row is not None else None
110	
111	
112	async def bin_exists(
113	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bin_id: uuid.UUID
114	) -> bool:
115	    """Whether a bin with ``bin_id`` exists in the tenant (PLAN 6.3). A goods receipt validates the
116	    target bin its stock lands in through this contract (D-029) rather than importing inventory
117	    models. Existence only — the move engine re-checks the bin is in an ACTIVE warehouse when it
118	    posts, so a receipt against an inactive-warehouse bin still fails (at post), loud."""
119	    stmt = select(Bin.id).where(Bin.tenant_id == tenant_id, Bin.id == bin_id)
120	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
121	
122	
123	async def default_bin_for_warehouse(
124	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
125	) -> uuid.UUID | None:
126	    """The default ACTIVE bin of a warehouse (or the lowest-coded active bin, or None) — PLAN 8.2,
127	    D-048. A production order pre-fills each exploded component row's source bin from this. Exposed
128	    so MANUFACTURING reads it downward (STRUCTURE §5) without importing inventory models."""
129	    stmt = (
130	        select(Bin.id)
131	        .where(
132	            Bin.tenant_id == tenant_id,
133	            Bin.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
134	            Bin.is_active.is_(True),
135	        )
136	        .order_by(Bin.is_default.desc(), Bin.code).limit(1)
137	    )
138	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
139	
140	
141	async def lot_id_for_code(
142	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID, lot_code: str
143	) -> uuid.UUID | None:
144	    """The id of an EXISTING lot for an item, by its lot_code (PLAN 7.3), or None. A sales delivery
145	    (an outbound ISSUE) must reference an existing lot by id — unlike a receipt, an issue never
146	    creates a lot — so the delivery resolves the human ``lot_code`` to a lot id through this
147	    contract (D-029) before issuing. Index-served by (tenant, item_id)."""
148	    stmt = select(Lot.id).where(
149	        Lot.tenant_id == tenant_id, Lot.item_id == item_id, Lot.lot_code == lot_code
150	    )
151	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
152	
153	
154	async def serial_id_for_code(
155	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID, serial_code: str
156	) -> uuid.UUID | None:
157	    """The id of an EXISTING serial for an item, by its serial_code (PLAN 7.3), or None. The serial
158	    twin of ``lot_id_for_code``: a delivery resolves a serial-tracked line's ``serial_code`` to a
159	    serial id before issuing (D-029). Index-served by (tenant, item_id)."""
160	    stmt = select(SerialNumber.id).where(
161	        SerialNumber.tenant_id == tenant_id,
162	        SerialNumber.item_id == item_id,
163	        SerialNumber.serial_code == serial_code,
164	    )
165	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
166	
167	
168	# --- On-hand projection reads (PLAN 5.2) --------------------------------------
169	# These read the MAINTAINED inv_stock_quants projection (D-036), kept in lock-step with the move
170	# ledger so on-hand is an indexed aggregate over a small current-state table, not a SUM over
171	# unbounded move history (PERFORMANCE §1). MoneyType/QuantityType propagation keeps the SUM exact on
172	# both engines (D-015); ``func.coalesce(..., 0)`` makes an item with no stock read 0, not None.
173	
174	
175	async def total_on_hand(
176	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
177	) -> Decimal:
178	    """Total on-hand quantity of an item across ALL bins and lots (PLAN 5.2). The number sales ATP
179	    starts from. Reads inv_stock_quants (the maintained projection), index-served by
180	    ``(tenant_id, item_id)``."""
181	    stmt = select(func.coalesce(func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty), 0)).where(
182	        StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id, StockQuant.item_id == item_id
183	    )
184	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()
185	
186	
187	async def on_hand(
188	    session: AsyncSession,
189	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
190	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
191	    bin_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
192	    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
193	) -> Decimal:
194	    """On-hand quantity of an item, optionally narrowed to one bin and/or one lot (PLAN 5.2). With
195	    no bin/lot this is ``total_on_hand``; with a bin it is that bin's stock; with a lot it is that
196	    lot's stock (in the bin if also given). Reads the maintained projection."""
197	    stmt = select(func.coalesce(func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty), 0)).where(
198	        StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id, StockQuant.item_id == item_id
199	    )
200	    if bin_id is not None:
201	        stmt = stmt.where(StockQuant.bin_id == bin_id)
202	    if lot_id is not None:
203	        stmt = stmt.where(StockQuant.lot_id == lot_id)
204	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()
205	
206	
207	async def items_below_reorder_point(
208	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
209	) -> list[tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal, Decimal, Decimal]]:
210	    """Items whose total on-hand is AT OR BELOW their reorder point (PLAN 6.4, D-042) — the
211	    consumption-based replenishment scan. Returns ``(item_id, on_hand, reorder_point,
212	    reorder_quantity)`` for each ACTIVE item that carries a positive reorder point, has a positive
213	    reorder quantity, and whose on-hand (the maintained ``inv_stock_quants`` projection, summed per
214	    item) has fallen to or under that point. Procurement's reorder scan turns each into a draft
215	    requisition line for ``reorder_quantity``.
216	
217	    SET-BASED (no per-item N+1, PERFORMANCE §2): the on-hand sum is a LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY over the
218	    quant projection (items with no stock read 0 via coalesce), and the reorder predicate filters in
219	    SQL. Inventory OWNS reorder_point/reorder_quantity (5.1); the DRAFT requisition is a procurement
220	    document (6.2) — this query is the contract procurement reads, never importing inventory
221	    models."""
222	    on_hand_sum = func.coalesce(func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty), 0)
223	    stmt = (
224	        select(
225	            Item.id,
226	            on_hand_sum.label("on_hand"),
227	            Item.reorder_point,
228	            Item.reorder_quantity,
229	        )
230	        .join(
231	            StockQuant,
232	            (StockQuant.tenant_id == Item.tenant_id) & (StockQuant.item_id == Item.id),
233	            isouter=True,
234	        )
235	        .where(
236	            Item.tenant_id == tenant_id,
237	            Item.is_active.is_(True),
238	            Item.reorder_point.is_not(None),
239	            Item.reorder_point > 0,
240	            Item.reorder_quantity.is_not(None),
241	            Item.reorder_quantity > 0,
242	        )
243	        .group_by(Item.id, Item.reorder_point, Item.reorder_quantity)
244	        .having(on_hand_sum <= Item.reorder_point)
245	        .order_by(Item.item_code)
246	    )
247	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
248	    return [
249	        (row[0], Decimal(row[1]), Decimal(row[2]), Decimal(row[3]))
250	        for row in rows
251	    ]
252	
253	
254	async def on_hand_by_bin(
255	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
256	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
257	    """Per-bin on-hand totals for an item (PLAN 5.2): ``{bin_id: qty}`` summed across that bin's
258	    lots. Bins with zero net stock are absent (the move service deletes a quant when it hits 0, so
259	    the projection holds only live stock). What a bin-level stock-overview screen reads."""
260	    stmt = (
261	        select(StockQuant.bin_id, func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty))
262	        .where(StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id, StockQuant.item_id == item_id)
263	        .group_by(StockQuant.bin_id)
264	    )
265	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
266	    return {row[0]: row[1] for row in rows}
267	
268	
269	async def on_hand_by_lot(
270	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
271	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
272	    """Per-lot on-hand totals for a LOT-tracked item (PLAN 5.2): ``{lot_id: qty}`` summed across
273	    bins. Quants with a NULL lot (fungible stock) are excluded — this view is for tracked items
274	    where lot traceability matters."""
275	    stmt = (
276	        select(StockQuant.lot_id, func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty))
277	        .where(
278	            StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id,
279	            StockQuant.item_id == item_id,
280	            StockQuant.lot_id.is_not(None),
281	        )
282	        .group_by(StockQuant.lot_id)
283	    )
284	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
285	    return {row[0]: row[1] for row in rows}
286	
287	
288	# --- Valuation reads (PLAN 5.3, D-020/D-037) ----------------------------------
289	# These read the VALUE SSOT (inv_item_valuations for moving-average, inv_cost_layers for FIFO), kept
290	# in lock-step with every move in the same transaction (D-037). The inventory-value dashboard KPI
291	# and
292	# valuation reports read these. MoneyType/QuantityType propagation keeps the SUMs exact (D-015).
293	
294	
295	async def item_value(
296	    session: AsyncSession,
297	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
298	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
299	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
300	) -> Decimal:
301	    """The current total inventory VALUE of an item (PLAN 5.3), optionally narrowed to one
302	    warehouse.
303	
304	    For a MOVING_AVERAGE item this sums ``inv_item_valuations.total_value``; for a FIFO item it sums
305	    ``remaining_qty × unit_cost`` over the live cost layers. An item uses exactly one method, so the
306	    other source contributes 0. The FIFO product is summed in PYTHON (each factor already a typed
307	    Decimal) rather than ``func.sum(qty × cost)``, because multiplying two scaled-integer columns on
308	    SQLite yields a ×10^12 value that the MoneyType result processor cannot un-scale (D-015 trigger
309	    discipline: SQL never multiplies two stored money/quantity columns)."""
310	    valuation_stmt = select(
311	        func.coalesce(func.sum(ItemValuation.total_value), 0)
312	    ).where(ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id, ItemValuation.item_id == item_id)
313	    layer_stmt = select(CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
314	        CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	        CostLayer.item_id == item_id,
316	        CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0,
317	    )
318	    if warehouse_id is not None:
319	        valuation_stmt = valuation_stmt.where(ItemValuation.warehouse_id == warehouse_id)
320	        layer_stmt = layer_stmt.where(CostLayer.warehouse_id == warehouse_id)
321	    mav_value = Decimal((await session.execute(valuation_stmt)).scalar_one())
322	    fifo_value = sum(
323	        (Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost) for qty, cost in (await session.execute(layer_stmt)).all()),
324	        Decimal(0),
325	    )
326	    return mav_value + fifo_value
327	
328	
329	async def valuation_summary(
330	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
331	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
332	    """Total inventory value per item across the tenant (PLAN 5.3): ``{item_id: value}`` — the
333	    moving-average totals plus the FIFO live-layer values, merged per item. What the inventory-value
334	    dashboard KPI sums. The moving-average totals are grouped in SQL; the FIFO layer products are
335	    summed in Python per item (D-015: no SQL multiply of two scaled money/quantity columns).
336	    PERFORMANCE §6: two reads, no per-item N+1."""
337	    mav_rows = (
338	        await session.execute(
339	            select(ItemValuation.item_id, func.sum(ItemValuation.total_value))
340	            .where(ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id)
341	            .group_by(ItemValuation.item_id)
342	        )
343	    ).all()
344	    layer_rows = (
345	        await session.execute(
346	            select(CostLayer.item_id, CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
347	                CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id, CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0
348	            )
349	        )
350	    ).all()
351	    totals: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
352	    for item_id_, value in mav_rows:
353	        if value is not None:
354	            totals[item_id_] = totals.get(item_id_, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(value)
355	    for item_id_, qty, cost in layer_rows:
356	        totals[item_id_] = totals.get(item_id_, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost)
357	    return totals
358	
359	
360	async def current_unit_cost(
361	    session: AsyncSession,
362	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
363	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
364	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
365	) -> Decimal:
366	    """The item's current per-unit BOOK cost in a warehouse (PLAN 5.4): the moving-average
367	    ``avg_unit_cost`` for a MOVING_AVERAGE item, or the weighted average of the live FIFO layers for
368	    a FIFO item — the SAME source a value-neutral transfer uses for its ledger cost
369	    (costing._current_unit_cost). A positive count variance enters stock at this cost so the value
370	    added matches the book cost (rather than an arbitrary entry price). Returns 0 when no
371	    valuation/layer exists yet (an item the system thinks is empty, counted positive — the
372	    adjustment then enters at 0 cost, a quantity-only correction with no value impact, which the
373	    operator can re-cost via a later receipt). The FIFO layer product is summed in PYTHON (D-015: no
374	    SQL multiply of two scaled money/quantity columns). One read for the MAV row, one for the FIFO
375	    layers (no per-layer N+1)."""
376	    valuation = (
377	        await session.execute(
378	            select(ItemValuation.avg_unit_cost).where(
379	                ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id,
380	                ItemValuation.item_id == item_id,
381	                ItemValuation.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
382	            )
383	        )
384	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
385	    if valuation is not None:
386	        return Decimal(valuation)
387	    rows = (
388	        await session.execute(
389	            select(CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
390	                CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id,
391	                CostLayer.item_id == item_id,
392	                CostLayer.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
393	                CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0,
394	            )
395	        )
396	    ).all()
397	    total_qty = sum((Decimal(qty) for qty, _cost in rows), Decimal(0))
398	    total_value = sum((Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost) for qty, cost in rows), Decimal(0))
399	    return (total_value / total_qty) if total_qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
400

1	"""Procurement's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Procurement sits above inventory (and finance) in the dependency order: the P2P documents in
4	6.2–6.4 (requisition → RFQ → PO → goods receipt → 3-way match) and finance AP reporting read THIS
5	file to resolve vendor state synchronously; procurement imports finance/queries + inventory/queries
6	downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is the ONLY procurement file
7	other modules import.
8	
9	The central D-029 link: finance AP stores a vendor on each bill/payment as an opaque ``partner_id``
10	(no FK). ``get_vendor_for_partner`` resolves that ``partner_id`` back to a ``Vendor`` so AP aging /
11	reporting can render the vendor's name and payment terms — the ``partner_id`` IS the ``Vendor.id``,
12	so it is a thin alias over ``get_vendor`` named for the reporting intent.
13	
14	PLAN 6.2 adds the PURCHASE-ORDER reads 6.3 (goods receipts) and 6.4 (the 3-way match) call:
15	``get_purchase_order``, ``po_line_open_quantity`` (ordered − received), ``get_po_for_receipt`` (the
16	header + lines a receipt needs) and ``open_po_lines_for_vendor`` (the awaiting-receipt worklist).
17	PLAN 7.2 adds ``open_incoming_quantity`` (ordered − received summed per item over live POs) — the
18	on-order side of sales ATP (D-044), a SANCTIONED cross-module read sales calls.
19	
20	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
21	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.

47	    stmt = select(Vendor).where(Vendor.tenant_id == tenant_id, Vendor.id == vendor_id)

131	async def po_line_open_quantity(
132	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_line_id: uuid.UUID
133	) -> Decimal | None:
134	    """The still-open quantity on a PO line — ordered minus received — or None if the line does not
135	    exist. 6.3 reads this to cap a goods receipt at the outstanding quantity; 6.4 reads it for the
136	    three-way match. Computed from the maintained ``received_quantity`` (raised by 6.3), so it is a
137	    point lookup, not a SUM over receipts."""
138	    line = (
139	        await session.execute(
140	            select(PurchaseOrderLine).where(
141	                PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
142	                PurchaseOrderLine.id == po_line_id,
143	            )
144	        )
145	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
146	    if line is None:
147	        return None
148	    return Decimal(str(line.quantity)) - Decimal(str(line.received_quantity))

151	async def get_po_for_receipt(
152	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_id: uuid.UUID
153	) -> tuple[PurchaseOrder, list[PurchaseOrderLine]] | None:
154	    """The PO header + its lines (item, ordered/received quantities, unit cost, tax code) — the data
155	    a goods receipt (6.3) needs to build receipt lines and a 3-way match (6.4) needs to compare.
156	    None when the PO is unknown to this tenant. Two indexed reads (header by PK, lines by
157	    (tenant, po_id)); no N+1 over lines."""
158	    po = await get_purchase_order(session, tenant_id, po_id)
159	    if po is None:
160	        return None
161	    lines = list(
162	        (
163	            await session.execute(
164	                select(PurchaseOrderLine)
165	                .where(
166	                    PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
167	                    PurchaseOrderLine.po_id == po_id,
168	                )
169	                .order_by(PurchaseOrderLine.line_number)
170	            )

172	        .scalars()
173	        .all()

191	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_id: uuid.UUID
192	) -> list[GoodsReceipt]:
193	    """Every goods receipt raised against a PO (PLAN 6.3), newest first — the per-PO receipt history
194	    the 6.4 three-way match reads to find what has been received. Index-served by
195	    (tenant, purchase_order_id)."""
196	    stmt = (
197	        select(GoodsReceipt)
198	        .where(
199	            GoodsReceipt.tenant_id == tenant_id,
200	            GoodsReceipt.purchase_order_id == po_id,
201	        )

207	async def po_line_open_to_bill(
208	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_line_id: uuid.UUID
209	) -> Decimal | None:
210	    """The still-open-to-bill quantity on a PO line — RECEIVED minus BILLED — or None if the line
211	    does not exist (PLAN 6.4, D-042). The 3-way over-billing constraint caps a match line at this:
212	    you can never bill beyond what was physically received (received_quantity is raised by 6.3
213	    goods receipts; billed_quantity by 6.4 matches). A point lookup on the maintained columns, not a
214	    SUM over matches."""
215	    line = (
216	        await session.execute(
217	            select(PurchaseOrderLine).where(
218	                PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
219	                PurchaseOrderLine.id == po_line_id,
220	            )
221	        )
222	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
223	    if line is None:
224	        return None
225	    return Decimal(str(line.received_quantity)) - Decimal(str(line.billed_quantity))

228	async def get_invoice_match(
229	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, match_id: uuid.UUID
230	) -> InvoiceMatch | None:
231	    """The invoice match with ``match_id`` in the tenant, or None (PLAN 6.4). A point lookup on the
232	    PK; lets another module (or reporting) read a match header without importing procurement service
233	    internals."""

235	        InvoiceMatch.tenant_id == tenant_id, InvoiceMatch.id == match_id
236	    )

240	async def matches_for_po(
241	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, po_id: uuid.UUID
242	) -> list[InvoiceMatch]:
243	    """Every invoice match raised against a PO (PLAN 6.4), newest first — the per-PO match history.
244	    Index-served by (tenant, purchase_order_id)."""
245	    stmt = (
246	        select(InvoiceMatch)
247	        .where(
248	            InvoiceMatch.tenant_id == tenant_id,
249	            InvoiceMatch.purchase_order_id == po_id,
250	        )
251	        .order_by(InvoiceMatch.created_at.desc())
252	    )
253	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
254	
255	
256	async def open_incoming_quantity(
257	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
258	) -> Decimal:
259	    """The total OPEN-INCOMING (on-order) quantity of an item across all live POs (PLAN 7.2, D-044)
260	    — the on-order side of sales ATP. Sums ``ordered − received`` over PO lines for ``item_id`` on
261	    SENT / APPROVED / PARTIALLY_RECEIVED orders (orders that are committed to the vendor and still
262	    expect goods). A DRAFT / PENDING / CANCELLED / fully-RECEIVED / CLOSED order contributes
263	    nothing.
264	
265	    SET-BASED (no per-PO N+1, PERFORMANCE §2): one join over PO lines filtered by the PO's status
266	    and
267	    a positive open quantity, summed in PYTHON over the (small) open set so the exact-decimal
268	    QuantityType round-trips identically on both engines (D-015: SQL never subtracts two scaled
269	    quantity columns for the result value). Exposed so sales reads the on-order figure without
270	    importing procurement models — the bottom-up cross-module read (STRUCTURE §5)."""
271	    stmt = (
272	        select(PurchaseOrderLine.quantity, PurchaseOrderLine.received_quantity)
273	        .join(
274	            PurchaseOrder,
275	            (PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == PurchaseOrder.tenant_id)
276	            & (PurchaseOrderLine.po_id == PurchaseOrder.id),
277	        )
278	        .where(
279	            PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
280	            PurchaseOrderLine.item_id == item_id,
281	            PurchaseOrder.status.in_(
282	                [
283	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.APPROVED.value,
284	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.SENT.value,
285	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_RECEIVED.value,
286	                ]
287	            ),
288	            PurchaseOrderLine.received_quantity < PurchaseOrderLine.quantity,
289	        )
290	    )
291	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
292	    return sum(
293	        (Decimal(str(ordered)) - Decimal(str(received)) for ordered, received in rows),
294	        Decimal(0),
295	    )
296	
297	
298	async def open_po_lines_for_vendor(
299	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
300	) -> list[PurchaseOrderLine]:
301	    """The still-open PO lines (ordered > received) on SENT / PARTIALLY_RECEIVED orders for a vendor
302	    — the receivable-against-vendor worklist 6.3 / 6.4 use to find what is awaiting receipt. Filters
303	    on the (tenant, vendor_id, status) index; the open-quantity test is a column comparison."""
304	    stmt = (
305	        select(PurchaseOrderLine)
306	        .join(
307	            PurchaseOrder,
308	            (PurchaseOrderLine.tenant_id == PurchaseOrder.tenant_id)
309	            & (PurchaseOrderLine.po_id == PurchaseOrder.id),
310	        )
311	        .where(
312	            PurchaseOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
313	            PurchaseOrder.vendor_id == vendor_id,
314	            PurchaseOrder.status.in_(
315	                [
316	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.SENT.value,
317	                    PurchaseOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_RECEIVED.value,
318	                ]
319	            ),
320	            PurchaseOrderLine.received_quantity < PurchaseOrderLine.quantity,
321	        )
322	        .order_by(PurchaseOrder.created_at, PurchaseOrderLine.line_number)
323	    )
324	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())

1	"""Production-order models (PLAN 8.2, parity PP production orders = FULL): the header, the exploded
2	component reservations, and the routing-snapshot operations.
3	
4	A production order turns COMPONENTS into a FINISHED parent item: a header (``ProductionOrder``) plus
5	its ``ProductionOrderComponent`` rows (the BOM exploded at create time — required vs issued
6	quantity) and its ``ProductionOrderOperation`` rows (the routing snapshotted for 8.3's capacity
7	load). The header mixes in ``DocumentMixin`` (it registers in core_documents + claims an MO- number
8	at creation — a posted document, unlike the 8.1 masters).
9	
10	All item/UoM/warehouse/bin ids are OPAQUE inventory ids (D-029): no cross-module FK to inventory
11	tables; the service validates each via ``inventory/queries`` before writing. The ``bom_id``/
12	``routing_id`` are INTRA-module composite tenant FKs to ``mfg_boms``/``mfg_routings`` (the exploded
13	version snapshots). Quantities use the D-015 QuantityType (scale-6, exact on both engines);
14	``accumulated_wip_cost`` uses MoneyType (the value side, quantized to currency).
15	
16	``accumulated_wip_cost`` is the running WIP debit for this order: raised by each component issue (by
17	the posted issue cost) and consumed at finish to compute the finished unit cost — the SSOT for the
18	WIP-nets-to-zero invariant (D-048), maintained on the header rather than recomputed from the journal
19	so the finish flow has the figure in hand.
20	"""

23	from datetime import date, datetime
24	from decimal import Decimal

43	class ProductionOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
44	    """A PRODUCTION ORDER HEADER (D-048): the order to produce ``quantity`` of ``item_id``.
45	
46	    ``item_id`` is the OPAQUE inventory parent item produced; ``bom_id`` is the INTRA-module BOM
47	    version EXPLODED into the component rows; ``routing_id`` (nullable) is the routing version
48	    snapshotted into the operation rows. ``warehouse_id`` is where components are issued FROM and
49	    the finished goods land. ``status`` runs the ``ProductionOrderStatus`` lifecycle.
50	    ``finished_quantity`` is raised at finish (0 until then); ``accumulated_wip_cost`` is the
51	    running WIP debit (raised by each issue, consumed at finish) — the WIP-nets-to-zero SSOT

1	"""Production-order DRAFT lifecycle (PLAN 8.2, D-048): create+explode, release, cancel + reads.
2	
3	The issue-to-WIP + finish-to-stock POSTING flows live in ``production_post.py`` (split at the
4	400-line cap, the sales delivery_post precedent); this file owns the DRAFT side. ``__init__``
5	re-exports both halves as one ``service`` surface.
6	
7	Rules enforced here (the service owns them, CLAUDE.md rule 7):
8	
9	- **create_production_order** — resolves the item's ACTIVE default BOM (or the supplied bom_id),
10	  EXPLODES its components into ``ProductionOrderComponent`` rows
11	  (required = quantity_per × order_qty × (1 + scrap_percent/100), quantized to the quantity scale),
12	  snapshots the active routing's operations into ``ProductionOrderOperation`` rows
13	  (planned_minutes = setup + run × order_qty), claims the gapless MO- number + registers the
14	  document, and validates the item is STOCKED, quantity > 0, the warehouse exists. SINGLE-LEVEL
15	  explosion: a sub-assembly component is itself produced by its OWN order (multi-level via
16	  references, D-047) — this order issues the sub-assembly as a finished material, it does not
17	  recurse.
18	- **release_order** — DRAFT→RELEASED; the component rows ARE the reservation (v1 ATP-style: release
19	  does NOT block on availability — a shortage is informational, the parity-doc backorder posture).
20	- **cancel_order** — DRAFT/RELEASED only; once a component is issued the order is POSTED-ish and
21	  must be FINISHED (issued stock + WIP cannot strand), so an IN_PROGRESS/FINISHED order is not
22	  cancellable.
23	"""

189	async def create_production_order(
190	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: ProductionOrderCreate
191	) -> ProductionOrder:
192	    """Create a DRAFT production order + EXPLODE its BOM into reserved component rows + SNAPSHOT
193	    its routing (D-048). Validates the parent item is STOCKED, quantity > 0 and the warehouse
194	    exists; resolves the BOM (active default unless supplied) and explodes required quantities
195	    (scrap-loaded, quantized); snapshots the routing operations' per-order load; registers the
196	    document + claims the MO- number. Born DRAFT — release reserves, issue consumes, finish
197	    produces."""
198	    quantity = Decimal(payload.quantity)
199	    if quantity <= 0:
200	        raise ValidationFailedError(
201	            message="Production quantity must be greater than zero",
202	            code="manufacturing.quantity_invalid",
203	            details={"quantity": str(quantity)},
204	        )
205	    await _require_stocked_item(session, tenant_id, payload.item_id)
206	    bom = await _resolve_bom(session, tenant_id, payload)
207	    routing = await _resolve_routing(session, tenant_id, payload)
208	    default_bin = await _default_bin(session, tenant_id, payload.warehouse_id)
209	    components = await mfg_queries.bom_components(session, tenant_id, bom.id)
210	    if not components:
211	        raise ValidationFailedError(
212	            message="The BOM has no components to explode",
213	            code="manufacturing.bom_no_components",
214	            details={"bom_id": str(bom.id)},
215	        )
216	
217	    order_id = uuid.uuid4()
218	    document = await docflow.register_document(
219	        session,
220	        tenant_id,
221	        PRODUCTION_ORDER_DOC_TYPE,
222	        order_id,
223	        doc_number=None,
224	        status=ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
225	    )
226	    await ensure_sequence(
227	        session,
228	        tenant_id,
229	        PRODUCTION_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME,
230	        PRODUCTION_ORDER_NUMBER_PREFIX,
231	        PRODUCTION_ORDER_NUMBER_PADDING,
232	        year_reset=True,
233	    )
234	    number = await claim_number(
235	        session, tenant_id, PRODUCTION_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=date.today()
236	    )
237	
238	    order = ProductionOrder(
239	        id=order_id,
240	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
241	        document_id=document.id,
242	        order_number=number,
243	        status=ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
244	        item_id=payload.item_id,
245	        quantity=quantity,
246	        bom_id=bom.id,
247	        routing_id=routing.id if routing is not None else None,
248	        warehouse_id=payload.warehouse_id,
249	        planned_start_date=payload.planned_start_date,
250	        planned_end_date=payload.planned_end_date,
251	        finished_quantity=Decimal(0),
252	        accumulated_wip_cost=Decimal(0),
253	        notes=payload.notes,
254	    )
255	    session.add(order)
256	    # The explosion factor scales component quantity_per (per the BOM's base_quantity) up to the
257	    # order quantity, then scrap loads each line. SINGLE-LEVEL: each direct component becomes one
258	    # reservation row — a sub-assembly is produced by its own order, this order consumes it as-is.
259	    base_quantity = Decimal(bom.base_quantity)
260	    for index, component in enumerate(components, start=1):
261	        scrap_factor = Decimal(1) + (Decimal(component.scrap_percent) / Decimal(100))
262	        required = _quantize_qty(
263	            (Decimal(component.quantity_per) * quantity / base_quantity) * scrap_factor
264	        )
265	        session.add(
266	            ProductionOrderComponent(
267	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
268	                production_order_id=order_id,
269	                line_number=index * 10,
270	                component_item_id=component.component_item_id,
271	                required_quantity=required,
272	                issued_quantity=Decimal(0),
273	                uom_id=component.uom_id,
274	                bin_id=default_bin,
275	            )
276	        )
277	
278	    if routing is not None:
279	        operations = await mfg_queries.routing_operations(session, tenant_id, routing.id)
280	        for operation in operations:
281	            planned = _quantize_qty(
282	                Decimal(operation.setup_time_minutes)
283	                + Decimal(operation.run_time_minutes_per_unit) * quantity
284	            )
285	            session.add(
286	                ProductionOrderOperation(
287	                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
288	                    production_order_id=order_id,
289	                    operation_number=operation.operation_number,
290	                    work_center_id=operation.work_center_id,
291	                    description=operation.description,
292	                    setup_time_minutes=Decimal(operation.setup_time_minutes),
293	                    run_time_minutes_per_unit=Decimal(operation.run_time_minutes_per_unit),
294	                    planned_minutes=planned,
295	                )
296	            )
297	
298	    await session.flush()
299	    await docflow.set_document_status(
300	        session,
301	        tenant_id,
302	        document.id,
303	        doc_number=number,
304	        status=ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
305	    )
306	    return order
307	
308	
309	async def release_order(
310	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
311	) -> ProductionOrder:
312	    """Release a DRAFT production order (D-048): DRAFT→RELEASED, materials reserved (the component
313	    rows ARE the reservation). Idempotent on an already-RELEASED order. The reservation does NOT
314	    block on availability — a shortage is informational (v1 ATP-style, the parity-doc backorder
315	    posture); a later phase can flag shortages without changing this transition. An IN_PROGRESS /
316	    FINISHED / CANCELLED order cannot be released."""
317	    order = await get_production_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
318	    status = ProductionOrderStatus(order.status)
319	    if status == ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED:
320	        return order
321	    if status != ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT:
322	        raise ConflictError(
323	            message=f"A {order.status} production order cannot be released",
324	            code="manufacturing.production_order_not_releasable",
325	            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
326	        )
327	    order.status = ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value
328	    order.released_at = datetime.now()
329	    await session.flush()
330	    await docflow.set_document_status(
331	        session, tenant_id, order.document_id, status=ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value
332	    )
333	    return order
334	
335	
336	async def cancel_order(
337	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
338	) -> ProductionOrder:
339	    """Cancel a DRAFT or RELEASED production order (D-048). Once a component has been issued the
340	    order is IN_PROGRESS — POSTED-ish: it has consumed stock to WIP, so it must be FINISHED (issued
341	    stock + WIP cannot strand; v1 has no reverse-issue), never cancelled. A FINISHED/CANCELLED order
342	    is terminal. Cancelling releases nothing physical (no component was issued)."""
343	    order = await get_production_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
344	    status = ProductionOrderStatus(order.status)
345	    if status not in (ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT, ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED):
346	        raise ConflictError(
347	            message=f"A {order.status} production order cannot be cancelled",
348	            code="manufacturing.production_order_not_cancellable",
349	            details={"order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
350	        )
351	    order.status = ProductionOrderStatus.CANCELLED.value
352	    await session.flush()
353	    await docflow.set_document_status(
354	        session, tenant_id, order.document_id, status=ProductionOrderStatus.CANCELLED.value
355	    )
356	    return order
357	
358	
359	async def list_production_orders(
360	    session: AsyncSession,
361	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
362	    *,
363	    item_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
364	    status: ProductionOrderStatus | None = None,
365	    cursor: str | None = None,
366	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
367	) -> Page[ProductionOrder]:
368	    """Keyset-paginated production orders ordered by order_number (D-014). The item/status filters
369	    narrow the set (index-served by (tenant, status) / (tenant, item_id)) and fold into the cursor
370	    fingerprint."""
371	    stmt = select(ProductionOrder).where(ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id)
372	    if item_id is not None:
373	        stmt = stmt.where(ProductionOrder.item_id == item_id)
374	    if status is not None:
375	        stmt = stmt.where(ProductionOrder.status == status.value)
376	    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(item_id, status)
377	    return await paginate(
378	        session,
379	        stmt,
380	        order_by=[OrderKey(ProductionOrder.order_number, SortDirection.ASC)],
381	        pk=ProductionOrder.id,
382	        cursor=cursor,
383	        limit=limit,
384	        filters=fingerprint,
385	    )

2	
3	A sibling sub-router under the same ``/api/v1/manufacturing`` prefix, mounted by
4	``router.include_router`` in router.py (the bom_router/routing_router precedent — ONE module
5	surface,
6	no second mount in main.py).
7	
8	RBAC (D-009; distinct authorities):
9	  - read by ``manufacturing.production_order.read``;
10	  - create+explode / cancel the order by ``manufacturing.production_order.manage``;
11	  - release (reserve materials) by ``manufacturing.production_order.release``;
12	- issue components + finish to stock by ``manufacturing.production_order.execute`` (both POST stock
13	    + WIP journals — the shop-floor action).
14	
15	Writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so the order + its N stock ISSUE/RECEIPT moves + N WIP
16	journals + the order update commit (or roll back) atomically; the document-creating + issue + finish
17	endpoints are IDEMPOTENT (D-013). The list is O(1) queries + paginated (PERFORMANCE §6).

1	"""Domain events manufacturing PUBLISHES (D-011/D-048). Declarative data only — no logic, no
2	models — so inventory's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py
3	allowance: an event carries no behaviour, so a subscriber in another module imports it without any
4	logic).
5	
6	These are the SANCTIONED cross-module mechanism for the production-order → stock-move effects
7	(D-048), mirroring procurement's ``GoodsReceiptPosted`` (6.3, the WIP-offset twin of the GR/IR
8	override) and sales' ``DeliveryShipped``/``ReturnReceived`` (7.3/7.4). Manufacturing OWNS the
9	production-order document; it MUST NOT call inventory's service directly (STRUCTURE §5). So:
10	
11	- ``ComponentsIssued`` (component ISSUE moves → Dr WIP / Cr Inventory): one ``ComponentIssueMove``
12	  per issued component line carries the item, the SOURCE bin, the quantity, optional lot/serial, and
13	  the ``wip_account_id`` — the valuation-offset OVERRIDE every move passes so the costing engine
14	  routes the ISSUE to WIP instead of COGS. The cost of the stock that left is COMPUTED by the
15	  costing engine (moving-average / FIFO), so no unit cost is on the event.
16	- ``OrderFinished`` (finished RECEIPT move → Dr Inventory / Cr WIP): one ``FinishedReceiptMove``
17	  (the parent item entering stock) carries the item, the DESTINATION bin, the finished quantity, the
18	  ``unit_cost`` = accumulated WIP / finished quantity (the goods enter at the WIP-accumulated cost),
19	  optional lot/serial CODES (a RECEIPT may create the master on the fly), and the ``wip_account_id``
20	  override so the costing posts Dr Inventory / Cr WIP.
21	
22	Inventory's ``handlers.py`` subscribes, creates each move via its OWN service with the WIP offset,
23	and links the production-order document → 'issued_to'/'finished_to' → move document. The handler
24	shares the session, so the moves + their WIP journals land in the SAME transaction as the
25	issue/finish — all-or-nothing (D-011/D-020): a closed period or insufficient stock rolls the WHOLE
26	issue/finish back.
27	
28	Manufacturing updates its OWN tables (the component ``issued_quantity``, the order
29	``accumulated_wip_cost``, ``finished_quantity``, status) in that same transaction; the order↔move
30	link is the durable docflow edge the handler writes, not a cross-module FK (D-048).
31	"""
32	
33	import uuid
34	from decimal import Decimal
35	from typing import ClassVar
36	
37	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
38	
39	from app.core.events import DomainEvent
40	from app.modules.manufacturing.constants import (
41	    COMPONENTS_ISSUED_EVENT_KEY,
42	    ORDER_FINISHED_EVENT_KEY,
43	)
44	
45	
46	class ComponentIssueMove(BaseModel):
47	    """One component line's worth of stock to ISSUE to WIP (D-048), the payload inventory's handler
48	    turns into a stock ISSUE move offset to WIP. Plain frozen data: the opaque component item +
49	    SOURCE bin ids (D-029), the quantity issued in the item's base UoM, and optional lot/serial IDS
50	    (the existing lot/serial the stock leaves on — an ISSUE references an existing instance by id,
51	    it creates none). No unit cost: the costing engine COMPUTES the cost of the stock that left."""
52	
53	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
54	
55	    item_id: uuid.UUID
56	    bin_id: uuid.UUID
57	    quantity: Decimal
58	    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
59	    serial_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
60	
61	
62	class ComponentsIssued(DomainEvent):
63	    """Production-order components were issued to WIP (D-048). Inventory's ``handlers.py``
64	    subscribes and creates one stock ISSUE move per ``move`` in the SAME transaction, each
65	    offsetting to ``wip_account_id`` (Dr WIP / Cr Inventory — the valuation-offset OVERRIDE, the 6.3
66	    GR/IR-override pattern applied to an ISSUE), and links the order document to each move document
67	    ('issued_to').
68	
69	    - ``production_order_id`` + ``order_number`` + ``document_id`` — the order document
70	      (``document_id`` is the core_documents id the handler links the move documents to).
71	    - ``warehouse_id`` — the warehouse the components issue FROM (each move's bin is in it).
72	    - ``move_date`` — the date the stock moves post on (ISO date string); a date in a CLOSED period
73	      makes each move's WIP journal trip the period trigger, rolling the whole issue back.
74	    - ``wip_account_id`` — the tenant's WIP clearing account (resolved by manufacturing from
75	      finance/queries before publishing); the valuation-offset OVERRIDE every move carries.
76	    - ``moves`` — the per-component issues (see ``ComponentIssueMove``)."""
77	
78	    key: ClassVar[str] = COMPONENTS_ISSUED_EVENT_KEY
79	
80	    production_order_id: uuid.UUID
81	    order_number: str
82	    document_id: uuid.UUID
83	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
84	    move_date: str
85	    wip_account_id: uuid.UUID
86	    moves: tuple[ComponentIssueMove, ...]
87	
88	
89	class FinishedReceiptMove(BaseModel):
90	    """The parent item's worth of stock to RECEIVE into finished goods (D-048), the payload
91	    inventory's handler turns into a stock RECEIPT move offset to WIP. Plain frozen data: the opaque
92	    parent item + DESTINATION bin ids (D-029), the finished quantity, the unit cost the goods enter
93	    at (= accumulated WIP / finished quantity, so the value entering inventory reconciles to WIP),
94	    and optional lot/serial CODES (a RECEIPT may create the lot/serial master on the fly for tracked
95	    items — unlike an issue which references one by id)."""
96	
97	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
98	
99	    item_id: uuid.UUID
100	    bin_id: uuid.UUID
101	    quantity: Decimal
102	    unit_cost: Decimal
103	    lot_code: str | None = None
104	    serial_code: str | None = None
105	
106	
107	class OrderFinished(DomainEvent):
108	    """A production order was finished to stock (D-048). Inventory's ``handlers.py`` subscribes and
109	    creates the finished-goods RECEIPT move in the SAME transaction, offsetting to
110	    ``wip_account_id`` (Dr Inventory / Cr WIP — the valuation-offset OVERRIDE), and links the order
111	    document to the move document ('finished_to'). The goods enter at the move's ``unit_cost``, so
112	    inventory value rises by the value credited out of WIP.
113	
114	    On the FINAL finish, ``variance_amount`` carries any residual WIP the finished receipt did NOT
115	    absorb (over/under-absorption — when the finished value differs from accumulated WIP). FINANCE's
116	    handler posts the variance entry (Dr/Cr WIP / Cr/Dr the variance account) so WIP nets to ZERO,
117	    the way finance posts the costing journal off StockValued — manufacturing never imports

2	update, cancel + reads.
3	
4	Lifecycle (constants.RequisitionStatus): DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED, or
5	DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED → CANCELLED, or APPROVED → CONVERTED (the convert services flip this). The
6	SUBMIT step evaluates the REQUISITION value-threshold rule on the estimated total
7	(Σ qty × estimated_unit_cost over the lines): at-or-above the active threshold the requisition STAYS
8	SUBMITTED awaiting an approver; below it the submit auto-advances to APPROVED (the data-driven rule,
9	D-040). A line without an estimate contributes 0 to the total — an all-estimate-less requisition has
10	total 0, which is below any positive threshold, so it auto-approves.
11	
12	The PR number is claimed AT CREATION (D-040) and the document is registered in core_documents then.
13	Idempotency (D-013) is owned by the endpoints.
14	"""

56	) -> PurchaseRequisition:

67	) -> list[PurchaseRequisitionLine]:

7	create financial documents.

10	assets — up to ``DEPRECIATION_RUN_SYNC_MAX_ASSETS`` (100) the run executes inline and returns
11	201 with the run; above that it submits a ``finance.depreciation_run`` job and returns
12	202 {job_id} for /api/v1/jobs polling. Both paths share one idempotent endpoint: the capture

144:## Production Planning (PP)
146:S/4HANA PP covers manufacturing master data (material master, multi-level BOMs, work centers, routings, production versions), demand management with planning strategies and planned independent requirements, MRP including the in-memory MRP Live engine, production order execution with shop floor control and confirmations, and capacity evaluation/leveling. It additionally ships lean/order-less execution models (kanban, repetitive manufacturing), process-industry variants (PP-PI), and embedded PP/DS for finite detailed scheduling and optimization. Atlas v1's plan covers the discrete-manufacturing core well (BOMs, work centers, routings, production orders with WIP accounting, a deterministic MRP run, rough capacity check) while deliberately omitting forecast-based demand management, operation-level confirmations, capacity leveling, kanban, repetitive manufacturing, PP-PI, and PP/DS-class finite scheduling — the same areas v1-grade systems typically defer.

Three tables (migration `0033_manufacturing_production`, down_revision 0032, no trigger-bearing alters, reversible, portable, ≤63-char ids): `mfg_production_orders` (DocumentMixin header + composite FKs to mfg_boms/mfg_routings), `mfg_production_order_components` (the exploded reservations), `mfg_production_order_operations` (the routing snapshot for 8.3 capacity load). **(a) Status lifecycle.** DRAFT (created + active BOM EXPLODED into component rows + routing snapshotted) → RELEASED (materials reserved — the component rows ARE the reservation, v1 ATP-style; release does NOT block on availability, a shortage is informational) → IN_PROGRESS (≥1 component issued to WIP) → FINISHED (parent fully produced, WIP nets to zero) | CANCELLED (DRAFT/RELEASED only — once a component is issued the order is POSTED-ish and must FINISH; issued stock + WIP cannot strand, no reverse-issue in v1). **(b) Single-level explosion.** `required_quantity = quantity_per × order_qty / base_quantity × (1 + scrap_percent/100)`, quantized to the QuantityType scale; a sub-assembly component is produced by its OWN order (multi-level via references, D-047), this order issues it as a finished material, it does not recurse. No active default BOM (and none supplied) → 422 `manufacturing.no_active_bom`. **(c) The §5 event-bus mechanism (the binding constraint).** Manufacturing imports ONLY `inventory/queries` + `finance/queries` + its own events — NEVER inventory/finance SERVICE (grep-verified). `issue_components` publishes `ComponentsIssued` → inventory's `handlers.issue_production_components` creates an ISSUE move per component with `valuation_offset_account_id` = the WIP account (the 6.3 GR/IR-override pattern applied to an ISSUE — required THREADING the override through the costing engine's outbound path `_apply_outbound`, which previously hardcoded the COGS offset) → the StockValued costing event posts Dr WIP / Cr Inventory. `finish_order` publishes `OrderFinished` → inventory's `handlers.receive_finished_order_move` creates a RECEIPT move (`unit_cost` = accumulated WIP / ordered qty, WIP offset) → Dr Inventory / Cr WIP. Both handlers register at `app.main.register_event_handlers` (the deterministic D-011 seam; the manufacturing test conftest re-registers after the per-test reset). **(d) accumulated_wip_cost tracking.** The order carries `accumulated_wip_cost` (MoneyType, the WIP-nets-to-zero SSOT): the issue flow raises it by the component's current book cost × qty (read pre-publish from `inventory/queries.current_unit_cost`, which equals the MAV issue cost the move will post — exact for moving-average), and the finish flow drains it. Maintained on the header (not recomputed from the journal) so the finish flow derives the finished unit cost in hand. Exposed via `manufacturing/queries.order_wip_balance`. **(e) The WIP-nets-to-zero invariant + the variance flush.** The finished goods enter at a UNIFORM per-unit cost = accumulated WIP / ordered qty (quantized); on the FINAL finish any residual (the quantization difference between accumulated WIP and the total received, or genuine over/under-absorption) is carried on `OrderFinished` as a SIGNED `variance_amount`, and finance's `post_production_variance` handler posts Dr/Cr WIP / Cr/Dr the production-variance account (the MAV zero-quantity-flush analogue) so the WIP clearing account nets to EXACTLY zero at completion. Routing the variance through a finance HANDLER (a second OrderFinished subscriber) — not a manufacturing-posted journal — keeps manufacturing free of any finance/service import (§5). Proven end-to-end: WIP balance == 0, the finished item's inventory value == the issued component cost, the residual holds in the variance account — read off the trial balance (the 6.4 GR/IR-clears-to-zero / 7.4 nets-to-zero precedent). **(f) Posting defaults.** `wip_clearing` (ASSET) + `production_variance` (EXPENSE) per-tenant posting defaults, resolved via NEW `finance/queries.wip_clearing_account` / `.production_variance_account` (the gr_ir/ppv mirror); an unmapped WIP account fails an issue/finish loud (422 `finance.posting_default_unmapped`). A closed period trips the WIP journal's period trigger in the same transaction and rolls the whole issue/finish back; insufficient stock trips the inventory move guard and rolls back (tests assert the rolled-back state via FRESH reads, never post-failure ORM state — issue #53). **(h) Permissions + numbering + structure.** `manufacturing.production_order` `.read` / `.manage` (create+cancel) / `.release` / `.execute` (issue+finish folded under one key — both POST stock+journals, the shop-floor action). # 5. Dependency Rules (what may import what)

- `core` imports nothing from `modules`. Modules import `core` freely.
- Modules never import each other's `service.py` or `models.py` directly. Cross-module effects go through the event bus (`finance/handlers.py` reacts to `inventory` events). Cross-module reads needed synchronously (e.g., sales needs an item's price) go through a small, explicit query interface the owning module exposes in `modules/<owner>/queries.py` — plus `modules/<owner>/events.py` (declarative event dataclasses only, no logic), the two files another module may import (events.py allowance added by D-011 so handlers can subscribe to typed events).
- Dependency direction for queries: finance is the bottom (everyone may use finance/queries), then inventory, then everything else. Two modules may never import each other's queries bidirectionally — if that seems needed, the shared concept is misplaced; file an issue and resolve ownership before coding.
- Frontend: `modules/*` may import `lib` and `components`; `components` and `lib` never import from `modules`.

# 6. Tests mirror source, exactly

`backend/tests/` replicates `app/` paths: code in `app/modules/finance/service/journal.py` is tested in `tests/modules/finance/test_journal.py`. Shared fixtures live in `tests/conftest.py` (db session, tenant factory, auth client) and `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` for module fixtures. Test names state the rule being proven: `test_journal_rejects_unbalanced_lines`, `test_posting_to_closed_period_raises`. One assertion-theme per test. Frontend tests sit beside the file they test (`DataGrid.test.tsx`). A regression test for issue #NN includes `#NN` in its docstring/comment.

# 7. Naming Conventions (single table of truth)

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Python files/modules | snake_case, singular concern | `journal.py`, `stock_move.py` |
| Python classes | PascalCase, no abbreviations | `JournalEntry`, `StockMove`, `PurchaseOrderLine` |
| Python functions/vars | snake_case verbs for actions | `post_journal_entry()`, `reserve_stock()` |
| Pydantic schemas | Entity + suffix `Create/Update/Read/Filter` | `JournalEntryCreate`, `ItemRead` |
| DB tables | snake_case plural, module prefix | `fin_journal_entries`, `inv_stock_moves`, `sls_orders` |
| DB columns | snake_case; FKs `<entity>_id`; money pairs `amount`+`currency_code`; booleans `is_/has_` | `is_posted`, `cost_center_id` |
| Enums (Py + DB values) | Class PascalCase, values UPPER_SNAKE stored as strings | `OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_SHIPPED` |
| Alembic revisions | `NNNN_short_description` sequential | `0007_add_asset_register` |
| Domain events | PascalCase past tense, module-prefixed string key | class `SalesOrderShipped`, key `sales.order.shipped` |
| Permissions | `module.entity.action` lowercase | `finance.journal.post` |
| API routes | `/api/v1/<module>/<resource-kebab-plural>`; actions as sub-resources, never verbs in resource names | `/api/v1/finance/journal-entries/{id}/post` |
| JSON fields | snake_case (mirror backend; frontend types match, no camelCase translation layer) | `posting_date` |
| TS files | Components PascalCase.tsx, everything else camelCase.ts | `DataGrid.tsx`, `apiClient.ts` |
| TS types/interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `JournalEntry` |
| React hooks | `use` + Entity + verb | `usePostJournalEntry` |
| CSS | Tailwind utilities only; the rare custom class kebab-case in one `index.css` | `doc-flow-edge` |
| Env vars | `ATLAS_` prefix UPPER_SNAKE | `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL` |
| Docs files | kebab-case | `industry-templates.md` |
| Branches/commits/labels | as defined in GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md | — |

Terminology lock: the same business concept uses the same word everywhere — code, DB, API, UI, docs. It is `item` (not product/article/sku interchangeably), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override the *display* label, never the internal name. Record any new canonical term in DECISIONS.md the moment you coin it.

# 8. File-Handling Rules

1. **Search before create.** Before creating any file, check whether its correct home already exists (`ls`, `grep -r "class JournalEntry"`). Duplicate implementations are a `severity:major` issue.
2. **No versioned filenames.** Never `service_v2.py`, `utils_new.py`, `final_fixed.tsx`. Improving a file means editing it; git holds history.
3. **No orphan files.** Every file is imported/referenced by something or it doesn't exist. When refactoring away from a file, delete it in the same commit.
4. **Size limits.** Hard cap 400 lines per Python file and 300 per TSX component; at the cap, split along the rules in §3/§4 — never split into `part1/part2`.
5. **One concept per file.** A file named `journal.py` containing tax logic is misfiled even if it compiles. Filename promises content.
6. **Generated files are never hand-edited** (OpenAPI dumps, lockfiles, migration auto-generations get reviewed and adjusted only through their tooling). Commit lockfiles; never commit build output, caches, coverage reports, or `__pycache__` — keep `.gitignore` authoritative.
7. **No utils graveyards.** Before adding to a `utils`-like file, ask which module/concern owns the function; `core/` files and `lib/format.ts` are the only sanctioned shared helpers, each scoped by its filename.
8. **Imports:** absolute imports only in backend (`from app.modules.finance.service import journal`); frontend uses the `@/` alias (`@/lib/apiClient`). No relative `../../..` chains.
9. **Module READMEs are forbidden** — module docs live in `docs/modules/<module>.md` only, so documentation has one home.
10. **Renames/moves** are their own commit (`refactor(structure): move costing into inventory/service/costing.py`), never mixed with logic changes, so history stays traceable.
11. **Deletions** follow issue-first if the file contains live logic being retired: file the issue, explain replacement, delete in the fix PR.
12. **After compaction:** before creating ANY new file, re-read this document and run `git status` + `tree -L 3` (or `find`) to re-anchor on the actual current structure. Never recreate from memory a file that might already exist.

# 9. Self-Check (append result to PROGRESS.md at each session end)

Any file outside the canonical tree? Any file over the size cap? Any duplicate concept names (`grep` a few suspects)? Any orphan files? Any module breaking the dependency rules? Any term drift (supplier vs vendor)? Each "yes" becomes a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6, fixed before the next promotion.

    """Lifecycle of a PLANNED ORDER (PLAN 8.3, D-049). The MRP run produces PLANNED proposals; a

    - CONVERTED: turned into a real production order / requisition (``converted_document_id`` links

    - CANCELLED: a planner discarded it. Terminal; a re-run keeps the row (history) but it adds no

"""MRP models (PLAN 8.3, parity PP MRP = PARTIAL): the run header, its regenerated planned orders,
and the rough-capacity-check load rows.

An MRP RUN (``MrpRun``) is the deterministic planning pass: it gathers DEMAND (open sales-order
demand + reorder-point shortfall) and SUPPLY (on-hand + open production orders + open POs) per item,
nets them, EXPLODES MAKE items' BOMs into dependent component demand level by level, and writes the
net plan as ``PlannedOrder`` rows (MAKE or BUY). The ``CapacityLoad`` rows are the rough capacity
check's per-work-centre output (planned + open load vs available hours over the horizon).

The run header mixes in ``DocumentMixin`` (it registers in core_documents + claims an MRP- number at
creation — a posted document, the depreciation-run precedent). Planned orders + capacity loads are
run-scoped OUTPUT, not documents: they carry no number and ride the run's audit story.

All item ids are OPAQUE inventory ids (D-029): no cross-module FK to inventory tables; the run reads
them through inventory/sales/procurement queries. ``mrp_run_id`` / ``work_center_id`` are INTRA-module
composite tenant FKs. Quantities use the D-015 QuantityType (scale-6, exact on both engines);
``utilization_percent`` is a QuantityType ratio (the efficiency_percent/scrap_percent precedent — a
plain Numeric loses precision on SQLite, D-015).
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
from app.core.models import (
    AuditMixin,
    Base,
    TenantMixin,
    TimestampMixin,
    UuidPKMixin,
    tenant_fk,
    tenant_unique,
)
from app.core.money import QuantityType
from app.modules.manufacturing.constants import (
    MrpRunStatus,
    PlannedOrderStatus,
    PlannedOrderType,
)


class MrpRun(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """An MRP RUN HEADER (D-049): one tenant-wide deterministic planning pass.

    ``warehouse_id`` is nullable — v1 MRP is TENANT-WIDE (on-hand summed across all warehouses,
    demand netted tenant-wide); the column reserves a warehouse-scoped run for a later phase
    (parity: MRP areas / multi-plant are deferred). ``run_date`` is the planning date; ``horizon_days``
    the netting/capacity window. ``planned_make_count`` / ``planned_buy_count`` summarize the plan.
    Registers a document + claims the gapless MRP- number at creation (D-012). Audited (D-010): a
    run drives downstream production/procurement proposals.
    """

    __tablename__ = "mfg_mrp_runs"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        document_fk(),
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id", "run_number", name="uq_mfg_mrp_runs_tenant_id_run_number"
        ),
        # The list filters on (tenant, status) and orders runs over time (PERFORMANCE §1).
        sa.Index("ix_mfg_mrp_runs_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
    )

    run_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20), nullable=False, default=MrpRunStatus.RUNNING.value, server_default="RUNNING"
    )
    run_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
    horizon_days: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False, server_default="30")
    # OPAQUE inventory warehouse id (D-029): NULL = tenant-wide (the v1 default). No FK to inv_*.
    warehouse_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    demand_source: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
    planned_make_count: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
    )
    planned_buy_count: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
    )
    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
    completed_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
    )


class PlannedOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """One PLANNED ORDER (D-049): a net replenishment proposal for ``quantity`` of ``item_id``.

    Produced by the run that owns it (``mrp_run_id``). ``order_type`` is MAKE (has an active BOM →
    convert to a production order) or BUY (no BOM → convert to a requisition). ``quantity`` is the
    NET requirement (max(0, demand − supply)). ``level`` is the BOM-explosion level (0 = a
    finished/demanded item, 1 = its components, …) — the run writes level-0 first, and reads/convert
    order by it. ``status`` runs the ``PlannedOrderStatus`` lifecycle; ``converted_document_id`` is
    the real document the conversion created (NULL until CONVERTED), linked via docflow.

    Regeneration (D-049): a re-run DELETES the prior PLANNED (un-firmed) rows for the tenant before
    writing fresh ones; FIRMED/CONVERTED/CANCELLED rows survive (FIRMED/CONVERTED net as supply).

    NOT AuditMixin: planning output rides the run header's audit story (the BomComponent /
    production-order-component precedent) — regenerated each run, no independent lifecycle worth a
    diff per row.
    """

    __tablename__ = "mfg_planned_orders"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("mfg_mrp_runs", "mrp_run_id"),
        sa.CheckConstraint("quantity > 0", name="ck_mfg_planned_orders_quantity_positive"),
        # The "this run's planned orders" read (the nested list, the capacity scan input).
        sa.Index("ix_mfg_planned_orders_tenant_id_mrp_run_id", "tenant_id", "mrp_run_id"),
        # The "an item's open planned orders by status" read (regeneration + the convert worklist).
        sa.Index(
            "ix_mfg_planned_orders_tenant_id_item_id_status",
            "tenant_id",
            "item_id",
            "status",
        ),
    )

    mrp_run_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    # OPAQUE inventory item id (D-029): the item to make/buy. No FK to inv_items.
    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    order_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(10), nullable=False)
    quantity: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
    due_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        sa.String(20),
        nullable=False,
        default=PlannedOrderStatus.PLANNED.value,
        server_default="PLANNED",
    )
    # The net-requirement explanation: "demand X − supply Y" (why this proposal exists).
    source_notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
    level: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0")
    # The production order / requisition document created on conversion (NULL until CONVERTED).
    # OPAQUE core_documents id (D-029-style): set by the convert flow, linked via docflow.
    converted_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)


class CapacityLoad(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """One work centre's ROUGH CAPACITY LOAD for an MRP run (D-049): the planned + open operation
    minutes routed through ``work_center_id`` compared to its available minutes over the horizon.

    ``planned_load_minutes`` = Σ planned-order operation minutes + open-production-order operation
    minutes through this work centre. ``available_minutes`` = capacity_hours_per_day × efficiency ×
    horizon_days × 60. ``utilization_percent`` = load / available × 100 (0 when available is 0).
    ``is_overloaded`` flags load > available. Evaluation only — no leveling/finite scheduling
    (parity: capacity = PARTIAL).

    NOT AuditMixin: run-scoped output, rides the run header's audit story.
    """

    __tablename__ = "mfg_capacity_loads"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("mfg_mrp_runs", "mrp_run_id"),
        tenant_fk("mfg_work_centers", "work_center_id"),
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "mrp_run_id",
            "work_center_id",
            name="uq_mfg_capacity_loads_tenant_run_work_center",
        ),
        sa.Index("ix_mfg_capacity_loads_tenant_id_mrp_run_id", "tenant_id", "mrp_run_id"),
    )

    mrp_run_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    work_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    planned_load_minutes: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(
        QuantityType(), nullable=False, default=Decimal(0), server_default="0"
    )
    available_minutes: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(
        QuantityType(), nullable=False, default=Decimal(0), server_default="0"
    )
    utilization_percent: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(
        QuantityType(), nullable=False, default=Decimal(0), server_default="0"
    )
    is_overloaded: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
    )

stmt = (
        select(ProductionOrder)
        .where(
            ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            ProductionOrder.status.in_(open_statuses),
        )
        .order_by(ProductionOrder.order_number)
    )
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())


# --- MRP supply + planned-order reads (PLAN 8.3, D-049) ------------------------


async def open_production_order_supply(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Decimal:
    """The UN-FINISHED quantity an item's OPEN production orders will yield (PLAN 8.3) — the
    in-house-supply side of the MRP net (the production analogue of procurement's
    ``open_incoming_quantity``). Sums ``quantity − finished_quantity`` over the item's
    DRAFT/RELEASED/IN_PROGRESS orders (a FINISHED/CANCELLED order yields nothing more). SET-BASED
    (no per-order N+1, PERFORMANCE §2): one filtered scan on (tenant, item_id), summed in PYTHON so
    the exact-decimal QuantityType round-trips identically on both engines (D-015)."""
    open_statuses = (
        ProductionOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
        ProductionOrderStatus.RELEASED.value,
        ProductionOrderStatus.IN_PROGRESS.value,
    )
    stmt = select(ProductionOrder.quantity, ProductionOrder.finished_quantity).where(
        ProductionOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
        ProductionOrder.item_id == item_id,
        ProductionOrder.status.in_(open_statuses),
    )
    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
    return sum(
        (Decimal(str(qty)) - Decimal(str(finished)) for qty, finished in rows),
        Decimal(0),
    )


async def get_mrp_run(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, run_id: uuid.UUID
) -> MrpRun | None:
    """The MRP run with ``run_id`` in the tenant, or None. A point lookup on the PK."""
    stmt = select(MrpRun).where(MrpRun.tenant_id == tenant_id, MrpRun.id == run_id)
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def planned_orders(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    mrp_run_id: uuid.UUID,
) -> list[PlannedOrder]:
    """A run's planned orders, ordered by (level, item) so finished goods (level 0) precede their
    components (PLAN 8.3). One indexed read by (tenant, mrp_run_id); the capacity scan + the nested
    list read these."""
    stmt = (
        select(PlannedOrder)
        .where(
            PlannedOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            PlannedOrder.mrp_run_id == mrp_run_id,
        )
        .order_by(PlannedOrder.level, PlannedOrder.item_id)
    )
    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())


async def planned_make_supply(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Decimal:
    """The quantity an item's still-open FIRMED/CONVERTED planned orders contribute as supply across
    ALL runs (PLAN 8.3, the regeneration policy, D-049). A FIRMED/CONVERTED planned order is a
    committed replenishment a fresh run must NOT re-propose — so the run nets it as supply.
    SET-BASED, summed in Python (D-015)."""
    stmt = select(PlannedOrder.quantity).where(
        PlannedOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
        PlannedOrder.item_id == item_id,
        PlannedOrder.status.in_(
            (PlannedOrderStatus.FIRMED.value, PlannedOrderStatus.CONVERTED.value)
        ),
    )
    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
    return sum((Decimal(str(qty)) for (qty,) in rows), Decimal(0))

Now the core MRP engine. This is the heart of the task. Let me think through the design carefully:

**Demand sources** (per item):
1. Open sales-order demand: `sales_queries.committed_quantity(item_id)` — sum of ordered − delivered over CONFIRMED/PARTIALLY_DELIVERED orders.
2. Reorder-point shortfall: `inventory_queries.items_below_reorder_point()` → demand = reorder_quantity.

**Supply sources** (per item):
1. On-hand: `inventory_queries.total_on_hand(item_id)`.
2. Open production orders: `mfg_queries.open_production_order_supply(item_id)`.
